job.description:
Location: WA-Seattle

Job Title:  Digital Content Producer - KIRO TV

 

Position Overview

KIRO 7 News is seeking a Digital Content Center Producer to help drive audience growth, maximize engagement, and lead our digital-first news strategy.

 

This role is central to how we cover breaking news, elevate enterprise journalism, and connect with audiences across web, mobile, OTT, search, and social platforms.

 

The ideal candidate is an expert in digital audience development, SEO, and content optimization, with strong editorial judgment and exceptional writing and editing skills. They understand how audiences discover news, what drives engagement and loyalty, and how to use analytics to make real-time content decisions. They thrive in fast-moving news environments, know how to identify high-impact stories, and can quickly adapt coverage strategies based on audience trends and performance data.

 

This is a hands-on, on-site role within the Content Center. Digital Content Center Producers collaborate closely with reporters, producers, photographers, and newsroom leadership to ensure KIRO 7 is first, fastest, and most accurate online while continuously expanding our digital audience and strengthening our position as Western Washington's leading local news source.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Monitor local and national news, field calls and tips, listen to police and emergency scanners, and track developing stories through public records and court systems.
  • Communicate and coordinate with newsroom staff and sources as stories develop.
  • Write, edit, and publish content across digital platforms including KIRO7.com, the mobile app, OTT, social media channels, and push alerts.
  • Develop and execute SEO strategies that improve search visibility, audience growth, and long-term content performance.
  • Optimize headlines, story structure, metadata, and distribution plans using SEO and audience insights.
  • Use analytics platforms including Chartbeat, Tableau, Google Trends, and social analytics tools to inform content decisions and identify growth opportunities.
  • Ensure daily content production and audience engagement goals are met.
  • Stream breaking news, major coverage events, and live newscasts.
  • Exercise strong editorial judgment during breaking news and high-volume coverage situations.
  • Identify opportunities to grow reach, engagement, and referral traffic through search, social, and emerging platforms.
  • Collaborate with newsroom teams to integrate digital storytelling into broadcast workflows and strengthen cross-platform coordination.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, Digital Media, Marketing, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Proven ability to manage breaking news and make sound editorial decisions in a fast-paced newsroom environment.
  • Exceptional writing, editing, headline writing, and copy-editing skills.
  • Strong understanding of audience development, content optimization, digital content strategy, and engagement best practices.
  • Demonstrated expertise in SEO, analytics platforms, CMS workflows, live streaming, and social publishing tools.
  • Experience using audience data and performance metrics to shape editorial decisions and drive measurable growth.
  • Deep understanding of AP Style, media law, and ethical journalism standards.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays, as news demands; this is an essential on-site role.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 3-5+ years of experience in a digital newsroom, audience development, or digital content strategy role.
  • Demonstrated success increasing website traffic, search rankings, audience engagement, or social growth through data-driven content decisions.
  • Experience managing SEO initiatives and developing strategies that improve organic search performance.
  • Experience coaching or leading newsroom staff on digital best practices, audience growth, and content optimization.
  • Familiarity with Google Analytics, Google Search Console, Google Trends, Chartbeat, Tableau, and other audience intelligence platforms.

The wage scale for this position is $24.75 per hour to $35.21 per hour. Final compensation for this role will be determined by a variety of factors such as skills, certifications, and relevant work experience.

job.title: Senior Manager, Platform Engineering and Delivery
job.description:
Who We Are:
SiriusXM and its brands (Pandora, SiriusXM Media, AdsWizz, Simplecast, and SiriusXM Connect) are leading a new era of audio entertainment and services by delivering the most compelling subscription and ad-supported audio entertainment experience for listeners -- in the car, at home, and anywhere on the go with connected devices. Our vision is to shape the future of audio, where everyone can be effortlessly connected to the voices, stories and music they love wherever they are.
 

This is the place where a diverse group of emerging talent and legends alike come to share authentic and purposeful songs, stories, sounds and insights through some of the best programming and technology in the world. Our critically acclaimed, industry-leading audio entertainment encompasses music, sports, comedy, news, talk, live events, and podcasting. No matter their individual role, each of our employees plays a vital part in bringing SiriusXM’s vision to life every day.
 

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, and the premier programmer and platform for subscription and digital advertising-supported audio products. SiriusXM’s platforms collectively reach approximately 150 million listeners, the largest digital audio audience across paid and free tiers in North America, and deliver music, sports, talk, news, comedy, entertainment and podcasts. Pandora, a subsidiary of SiriusXM, is the largest ad-supported audio entertainment streaming service in the U.S. SiriusXM's subsidiaries Simplecast and AdsWizz make it a leader in podcast hosting, production, distribution, analytics and monetization. The Company’s advertising sales organization, which operates as SiriusXM Media, leverages its scale, cross-platform sales organization and ad tech capabilities to deliver results for audio creators and advertisers. SiriusXM, through SiriusXM Canada Holdings, Inc., also offers satellite radio and audio entertainment in Canada. In addition to its audio entertainment businesses, SiriusXM offers connected vehicle services to automakers.

How you’ll make an impact:

As Senior Manager, Platform Engineering & Delivery, you will be a hands-on technical leader responsible for advancing how software is built, tested, secured, packaged, and delivered across SiriusXM. You will lead the Delivery team while remaining actively engaged in architecture, engineering design, prototyping, technical reviews, and solving complex delivery challenges alongside the engineers you lead.

You will also be advancing Agentic Delivery: evolving our software delivery platform so AI agents can perform increasingly complex parts of the software development lifecycle—including coding, testing, validation, remediation, and delivery—based on human direction and within well-defined engineering, security, and operational guardrails. You will help define the architecture, platform capabilities, standards, and controls required to make agent-driven software delivery safe, reliable, observable, and scalable across the enterprise.

You will also own and evolve the foundational delivery capabilities that engineering teams and agents depend on, including CI/CD, artifact management, code quality, software supply chain security, and security scanning in CI pipelines. Your goal will be to create a delivery platform that makes the secure and reliable path the easiest path, whether the work is being performed by a human engineer, an AI agent, or a combination of both.

This is a player-coach role. You will provide people leadership and strategic direction, but you will also be expected to stay close to the technology, evaluate and improve technical designs, contribute to technical solutions, and directly help move important initiatives forward.

What you’ll do:

  • Lead the evolution toward Agentic Delivery: Define and execute the technical strategy for enabling AI agents to safely perform software delivery work based on human intent. Build the platform capabilities, APIs, workflows, context, permissions, feedback loops, and guardrails needed for agents to write code, run tests, remediate issues, validate changes, and progress software through delivery workflows.

  • Remain hands-on technically: Work directly with engineers on architecture, system design, prototypes, technical investigations, and complex implementation challenges. Review code and designs where appropriate, validate technical approaches, and help establish reference implementations for new delivery capabilities.

  • Own the software delivery architecture: Set technical direction across CI/CD, artifact management, code quality, software supply chain controls, and security scanning in CI pipelines. Ensure these capabilities work together as a coherent delivery platform rather than as disconnected tools.

  • Design for both human and agent consumers: Evolve delivery systems so workflows can be used consistently through developer interfaces, APIs, automation, and AI agents. Ensure delivery capabilities expose the context, controls, telemetry, and machine-readable interfaces required for increasingly autonomous engineering workflows.

  • Create secure, reusable paved paths: Develop and drive adoption of standardized delivery patterns that reduce one-off implementations, improve developer productivity, and embed security, compliance, reliability, and observability into the default workflow.

  • Advance CI/CD and release engineering: Improve development feedback loops, pipeline performance, release reliability, and consistency across engineering teams. Identify bottlenecks and use automation, platform engineering, and AI where appropriate to remove unnecessary manual work.

  • Strengthen software supply chain security: Partner with Information Security to integrate code scanning, dependency controls, artifact integrity, vulnerability management, provenance, policy enforcement, and other secure-by-default controls directly into CI pipelines and delivery workflows.

  • Standardize artifacts: Establish scalable patterns for how packages and build outputs are created, secured, stored, promoted, traced, and consumed across environments.

  • Use engineering data to drive improvement: Establish metrics around pipeline performance, adoption, failure rates, developer wait time, release reliability, agent effectiveness, remediation outcomes, and other delivery signals. Use those metrics to prioritize platform improvements and measure their impact.

  • Lead and develop the Delivery team: Provide clear technical and organizational direction, coach engineers and technical leads, build leadership capability, manage performance, and create an environment where engineers can take meaningful ownership of complex platform problems.

  • Drive cross-functional technical alignment: Work closely with Developer Experience, Cloud, Observability, Information Security, application engineering, and other stakeholders to solve cross-cutting delivery problems and establish common engineering standards.

  • Own roadmap and investment decisions: Translate engineering and business needs into a prioritized roadmap, balancing strategic platform investment, operational reliability, technical debt, developer productivity, security, and cost.

  • Evaluate emerging technologies pragmatically: Continuously assess new approaches in AI-assisted development, agentic engineering, CI/CD, software supply chain security, and developer tooling. Prototype where appropriate and turn successful experiments into production-grade platform capabilities.

What you’ll need:

  • Typically 7 or more years of software engineering or platform engineering experience, including 3 or more years leading engineering teams or technical organizations.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Strong hands-on technical background. You should be comfortable going deep on architecture, reviewing technical designs, reading and reviewing code, building prototypes, debugging complex systems, and working directly with engineers to solve difficult platform problems.

  • Experience designing modern software delivery systems, with strong knowledge of one or more of the following: CI/CD platforms, GitHub Actions or similar workflow systems, artifact repositories, developer tooling, code quality platforms, software supply chain security, or security scanning in CI pipelines.

  • Strong software engineering skills. Experience designing and building production software, automation, APIs, platform services, or developer tooling in one or more modern programming languages.

  • Experience with AI-assisted or agentic software development. Understanding of how coding agents, LLM-based engineering tools, tool-calling agents, or similar systems can participate in the software development lifecycle. Experience building or integrating agentic workflows is strongly preferred.

  • Ability to reason about the architecture of Agentic Delivery systems, including context and tool access, permissions, human approval points, policy enforcement, isolation, auditability, observability, feedback loops, and safe execution of autonomous actions.

  • Deep understanding of CI/CD and software delivery architecture, including build and test automation, security scanning in CI pipelines, release workflows, artifact promotion, environment management, deployment patterns, and the operational concerns associated with running these systems at enterprise scale.

  • Strong understanding of software supply chain security, including secure build practices, dependency and vulnerability management, artifact integrity, provenance, policy enforcement, and shifting security controls earlier in the development lifecycle through CI pipelines.

  • Strong cloud and platform engineering fundamentals, preferably with experience operating large-scale systems on AWS and working with infrastructure-as-code and distributed systems.

  • Technical leadership and judgment. Ability to make architecture decisions, evaluate technical designs and trade-offs, identify where standardization creates leverage, balance short- and long-term considerations, and guide engineers through ambiguous technical problems.

  • People leadership. Proven ability to coach and develop engineers and technical leads, manage performance, build healthy teams, delegate effectively, and develop future technical and organizational leaders.

  • Cross-functional influence. Ability to work effectively with engineering, infrastructure, security, product, and senior leadership; communicate complex technical topics clearly; and drive adoption of standards across teams you do not directly manage.

  • Operational and product mindset. Ability to treat internal platform capabilities as products, measure adoption and outcomes, understand developer needs, prioritize based on impact, and continuously improve the experience of engineers using the platform.

  • Must have legal right to work in the U.S.

At SiriusXM, we carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including your background and experience. These considerations can cause your compensation to vary. We expect the base salary for this position to be in the range of $106,600 to $190,000 and will depend on your skills, qualifications, and experience. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary short-term and long-term incentives. We encourage all interested candidates to apply.

job.title: Senior Video Editor, Reporter Video
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is an industry leader in visual journalism with reporting that includes extraordinary news coverage, investigations, culture and lifestyle reporting. The Reporter Video team identifies compelling stories and brings the depth and breadth of our news report onto our site and other platforms through video that features the expertise of our world-class journalists.

We are looking for an experienced video editor with a portfolio that demonstrates the ability to deliver engaging work on tight deadlines. You will work across a range of newsroom video coverage focused on vertical video storytelling with The Times' world-class journalists on-camera. You have deep experience in breaking and ongoing news coverage, with a track record of creating digitally compelling short-form video journalism.

Your portfolio and work samples should reveal a strong grasp of modern mobile video storytelling, and it should show that you're a quick learner with creative ideas and the ability to work on small or large teams. You are collaborative and solid technically with a solutions mindset, detail oriented, organized and fast.

Please note we have two positions available in the newsroom. Please speak to your expertise and/or interest(s) in your cover letter:

  • News and Enterprise

  • Culture and Lifestyle (music and film to fashion and real estate)

These are in-office positions based in New York and include regular attendance in the office four days each week. We are open to a Senior Video Editor working out of our LA office for the News and Enterprise role only. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Video editing and color correction of news, culture, enterprise and investigative videos featuring reporters from across the newsroom.

  • Collaborate with video journalists and producers in the pre/post production process, including writing, structure and creative execution. Demonstrate excellent news judgment across projects.

  • Deliver top-notch product under intense deadline pressure, and without the need for direct supervision, continuous editorial guidance, or task management.

  • Work across a range of stories with various newsroom desks including culture and styles, often juggling multiple projects.

  • Work with animators to incorporate animation, motion graphics and house design styles into videos.

  • Experiment with different formats of vertical and mobile visual storytelling.

  • Guide junior staff on edits as needed.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to a Senior Producer based in New York.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of multimedia storytelling, video editing and production experience at a major news video outlet and/or production company. (Minimum 5 years of video editing experience.)

  • Strong digital video editing background.

  • Expertise in Adobe Premiere and Creative Suite.

  • Strong audio editing, mixing and fixing skills for video.

  • Proven ability to craft stories, own video research for a project and edit a video with oversight from managers and senior staff.

  • Thorough knowledge of current events, with experience covering news.

  • The ability to conceive and create fresh original videos related to the news.

  • Must have an impressive portfolio of video editing primarily for digital or broadcast.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience animating and editing animations in Adobe After Effects.

  • A digital first mindset to editing on-platform and for social media.

  • Familiarity with the latest video editing techniques and technologies.

  • The ability to make quick decisions under intense deadlines in a high-pressure newsroom setting.

  • A foundational knowledge of legal, ethical, copyright and usage issues for visuals.

  • Well-versed in the world of social and digital media, with a keen eye on what competitors are doing and what new tools are being used.

  • Willingness to work evenings and weekends.

job.title: Sr. Creative Recruiter
job.description:
Who We Are

UnitedMasters is building a marketplace that connects artists, brands and fans - empowering over 1.5M artists to earn and grow. UnitedMasters has taken the bold step of building a music distribution service that, radically, puts artists first - disrupting the legacy music business by letting up-and-coming artists distribute their music directly to fans through streaming services while maintaining ownership of their master recording rights and up to 100% of royalties. Through the combination of UnitedMasters’ music distribution platform and its deep ties to brands, UnitedMasters enables independent artists to grow and earn unlike any other platform. 

Its unrivaled monetization opportunities for artists are amplified by Translation, UnitedMasters’ in-house creative marketing agency renowned for helping ambitious brands thrive in contemporary culture. In 2022, Translation was awarded the number three spot in Ad Age’s Agency A-List and AdWeek’s Multicultural Agency of the Year. One year before, Translation was awarded Ad Age’s Small Agency of the Year. 

We’re looking for a Sr. Creative Recruiter to join our team and support hiring for Translation, our creative advertising agency that partners with some of the world’s most recognized brands.

Full-Cycle Recruiting

  • Manage the end-to-end recruiting process across a wide variety of corporate, technical, creative, and business roles.
  • Partner with hiring managers to define hiring strategies, interview plans, and ideal candidate profiles.
  • Build and maintain strong candidate pipelines through sourcing, networking, referrals, and market research.
  • Deliver an exceptional candidate experience from initial outreach through offer acceptance.
  • Manage multiple searches simultaneously while maintaining speed, quality, and communication.

  • Act as a strategic advisor to hiring managers throughout the recruiting process.
  • Provide market insights, compensation guidance, and hiring recommendations.
  • Facilitate interview calibration and drive effective hiring decisions.
  • Influence stakeholders to ensure an efficient, high-quality hiring process.

Sourcing & Pipeline Development

  • Proactively source passive talent using LinkedIn Recruiter, networking, referrals, and creative sourcing strategies.
  • Develop diverse talent pipelines for current and future hiring needs.
  • Build relationships with candidates across creative, technical, and business disciplines.

Recruiting Operations

  • Maintain accurate recruiting data within the applicant tracking system.
  • Track recruiting metrics including time-to-fill, pipeline health, and offer acceptance rates.
  • Recommend process improvements that enhance efficiency and candidate experience.
  • Support employer branding initiatives, recruiting events, and talent community engagement.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Ability to recruit a mix of corporate, technical, and creative talent.
  • Strong sourcing skills with demonstrated success attracting passive candidates.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritize competing searches in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience using Greenhouse or another ATS.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Data-driven approach to recruiting and process improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 4+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience within an advertising agency 
  • Proven track record of hiring high-performing talent across multiple functions and levels, including senior-level roles

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ADP, Greenhouse, and Google suite preferred

About UnitedMasters, Inc.

UnitedMasters has over 1.5 million artists on its platform and is growing rapidly. Brands like Diageo, Ally, and ESPN come to UnitedMasters to partner with these artists and play a role in moving culture forward. In the past year, UnitedMasters subscribers have grown rapidly. With $170M raised to date and valued at $550M, UnitedMasters is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Apple, Alphabet (aka Google), and Disney amongst others. Over the last year, UnitedMasters artists have used our platform to land sync deals with major brands including the NBA, ESPN, Overtime Elite, Bose, Warner Brother Studios and in the NBA video game 2k. These deals give them additional money for their work and increase their exposure.

job.title: Editor, Cannonball
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for an experienced, imaginative senior editor to lead Wesley Morris's weekly culture show, Cannonball, which debuted in 2025. This role is fundamentally about partnership: working closely with one of the great cultural critics of our time to keep developing the show and reaching new heights; and leading a small team of producers to translate Wesley's critical voice, instincts, and curiosity into a show that feels as engaging as it is intellectually sharp.

The show's format is loose and conversational. Episodes are built around Wesley's exchanges with fellow critics, artists, and cultural figures; at their best they feel real, incisive, intimate, surprising, loose, unpredictable and crackling with on-the-fly cultural criticism. The senior editor will play a key role in refining this format, ensuring that each episode feels cohesive, dynamic, and fun while showcasing the distinct voice and authority that define Wesley's work.

This job is for you if: you are a rigorous editor, a strong producer and an active, generative collaborator — someone who can listen as well as direct. You enjoy the give and take involved in challenging, sharpening, and expanding ideas in real time with a dynamic team. You know and have respect for Wesley's critical voice. You are an experienced and accomplished culture editor/writer/producer/thinker in your own right, someone with ideas about what's going on in the world of movies, TV, books, music, art and more. You have a keen sense of who the interesting critical voices in this landscape are, and a sense of how to program great guests each week. You are well-organized, someone capable of leading a multidisciplinary team through the many overlapping stages of development and production on multiple episodes at a time. You're adept at working within a larger editorial system, taking notes and other input. You have an understanding of YouTube and other social platforms where the show may travel. You have a feel for the right way to use audience data to inform editorial decision-making. You're adaptable, friendly, creative, and discerning. And above all, you're interested in and capable of doing all the work—both the glamorous and exciting stuff and the basic but necessary stuff—to build a successful show.

As senior editor of Cannonball, you will also be part of the staff of The New York Times Magazine, where Wesley is a staff writer and where the show is based. You will draw on and be part of the magazine's cultural coverage.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as an editorial partner to Wesley Morris, shaping episode ideas, refining arguments, and helping translate his voice and sensibility into a compelling episode.
  • Come up with interesting ideas for guests and manage the process of bringing them in and staging successful conversations with Wesley.
  • Lead the editorial process from pitch through final cut, including story development, scripting, structural editing, and post-production feedback.
  • Collaborate with producers, editors, and Magazine and Shows leadership to ensure editorial clarity, creative ambition, and high production quality across every episode.
  • Manage and mentor a multidisciplinary team, setting clear expectations, providing feedback, and fostering a collaborative, high-performing culture.
  • Oversee production timelines and workflows, ensuring deadlines are met without compromising quality or ambition.
  • Maintain a strong, consistent editorial voice while pushing the show to expand creatively and reach new audiences.
  • Develop new formats and concepts for a show that's still evolving.
  • Work with Magazine leadership to integrate the show into the Magazine's editorial plans, voice and design, helping the show grow into a recurring, high‑impact Magazine franchise.
  • Partner with audience, analytics, and platform teams to understand viewer and listener behavior and refine the show's format, distribution, and growth strategy.
  • Work cross-functionally with other newsroom desks and teams to identify opportunities for collaboration, guest booking, and editorial alignment.
  • Work proactively with Legal and Standards departments to keep the show free of corrections and/or legal challenges.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Magazine's Deputy Editor overseeing Culture.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience editing/producing cultural coverage—criticism, cultural reporting, and storytelling in a variety of formats.
  • 5+ years experience in audio and/or video production and editing, including managing soup‑to‑nuts production of long‑form, conversational shows.
  • Deep interest in movies, TV, books, music, art, and all forms of culture (both rarefied/literary and pop).
  • Sophisticated sense of how criticism can work to open up, explore and define a work of art by reading it closely, putting it in larger context, and registering a personal response to it.
  • Sharp instincts for the ways that ideas about culture intersect with everything else: politics, history, technology, identity, business, and everyday life.
  • Familiarity with digital storytelling formats.
  • Experience working with talent.
  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing — from structuring episodes and pacing to line editing and shaping host conversations to guiding group edits and editorial brainstorms.
  • Belief in The New York Times's mission and a strong commitment to journalistic independence, fairness and accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience with a weekly publishing cadence and in managing teams under deadline.
  • 5+ years experience managing teams, including setting expectations, giving feedback and supporting people's growth.
  • Proven ability to foster an inclusive, diverse and innovative environment, both on‑air and within the team.
  • Deep familiarity with vertical video platforms and the changing social media landscape.
  • Knowledge of YouTube and social video strategy, or a demonstrated ability to learn and apply platform best practices in partnership with audience and video colleagues.
  • Experience in Adobe Premiere.

  • Experiment with various forms of short-form vertical video storytelling.

  • Excellent news judgment and proven ability to work with colleagues and reporters to synthesize newsgathering and/or investigations into a tight, informative and engaging video.

  • Experience producing shoots and interviewing experts on camera.

  • Experience creating original videos that intelligently incorporate audio, video, still images and text.

  • Strong video editing skills with Adobe Premiere.

  • Facility in using photo, video, audio, graphics and animation in storytelling.

  • Design and animation skills including experience with design and animation software (Figma, Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects).

Overview

Job Title: Promotions Assistant 

 

Department: Promotions

 

Reporting To: Promotions Director

 

Employment Type:    Part-Time

 

Location(s):  Richmond, VA

Work Arrangement: On-Site/Activation

 

Overview:

 

Audacy Richmond is looking for ambitious, energetic, and outgoing individuals to join our Promotions team! 

 

This is a part-time, flex schedule position with a great organization that allows you to get your foot in the door in a fast-paced, industry-leading, media company. The Promotions Assistant/Street Team position is unlike any other – this market allows the opportunity to both showcase and enhance a multitude of desired skill sets including in-field marketing, event production, live broadcast assistance, photography, videography, editing, social media coordination, office assistance and more. You'll be the face, heart, and soul of four powerful brands serving at the forefront of listener interactions, concerts, sport and lifestyle events, and much more.

 

 

Pay Transparency:

 

The anticipated starting salary range for Richmond-based individuals expressing interest in this position is $15.00/Hr..

 

Salary to be determined by the education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities and location of the applicant, as well as internal and external equity.

Audacy offers full time employees with a comprehensive benefits package to include:  health care coordinator, medical, dental, vision, telemedicine, flexible spending accounts, health savings account, disability, life insurance, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, paid time off (sick, vacation, personal, parental, volunteer), 401(k) retirement plan, discounted employee stock purchase, student loan payment assistance program, legal assistance, life assistance program, identity theft protection, discounted home and auto insurance, and pet insurance.

 

Responsibilities

 

What You'll Do:

 

Our Promotions Assistant/Street Team is responsible for spreading the word and passion for our stations and brands to the masses by taking to the street! You will assist with everything from in-office support such as preparing and executing on-air, online, and on-site contests, contacting winners, processing winner paperwork, and more, to working live events, appearances, and remote broadcasts assisting with setup, teardown, on-site activations, audio/video equipment, driving station vehicles, and more! We are looking for energetic, dependable, flexible team members who use sound judgment and have an outgoing personality that are ready to roll up their sleeves, learn, work hard, and have fun doing it! If you love music, sports, entertainment, culture, and you have a knack for "figuring it" and "getting it done", we have a team ready to enhance and improve your skills while providing an opportunity to learn and grow in a fast-paced industry. The Promotions Assistant/Street Team is responsible for the following, including but not limited to: 

  • Execute on-site promotional events and coordinate/manage clients and listeners on-site.
  • Set up, break down, and transport promotional event equipment as required.
  • Set up and run audio and other types of equipment during an event.
  • Hang banners and other staging elements at events.
  • Record events (ex. photos, videos, and audio) for purposes such as social media platforms and

recap of the event.

  • Responsible for fulfilling winner release forms and other waivers when needed for an event.
  • Maintain promotional equipment and vehicles in a clean and neat manner;
  • Check email daily; attend mandatory meetings on time; be able to work weekends, holidays, and

blackout dates (specified by Promotions Director/Manager).

  • Must be available to work Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays
  • May need to work with little notice.
  • Must be 18 or older.

 

Qualifications

Required & Preferred:

 

Required:

  • A positive attitude, and willingness to be a team player.
  • A valid driver's license, satisfactory completion of a motor vehicle record check, and, if the position requires use of the applicant's own vehicle, proof of insurance is required.
  • Ability to drive company vehicles to and from events.
  • Ability to lift and/or carry equipment.
  • Professional appearance and punctuality.
  • Reliable and dependable mode of transportation.
  • High School Diploma or GED.

 

Preferred:

 

  • Experience using Google Workspaces (Gmail, Google Drive, Google Calendar, etc.) is a plus
  • Knowledge of promotions software, including but not limited to Vibes (mobile contesting),
  • Aptivada (web contesting and user-generated content engine) and PromoSuite (promotion management software) a plus.
  • Experience working with the general public is preferred.

 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs and/or ladders; balance; stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl; talk, hear or smell. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 35 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

Important Notes:

Please be aware that Audacy will never ask you to send money at any point during the hiring process. Communication from legitimate Audacy representatives will only come from email addresses ending in @audacy.com. If you receive any suspicious requests or communications, please verify their authenticity before responding.

About Us

Audacy is a leading audio content and entertainment company. As champions of audio, we connect with people in the moments that matter — delivering trusted local news, passionate sports and your favorite music across 220+ radio stations, premium podcasts, live events and digital experiences that reach more than 200 million listeners every month.We create compelling content, foster deeply engaged audiences and deliver outcomes that matter for advertisers. Learn more at www.audacyinc.com and join the conversation on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

To request a reasonable accommodation for this purpose, please call 1-610-660-5614. job.description:
At Warner Music Group, we’re a global collective of music makers and music lovers, tech innovators and inspired entrepreneurs, game-changing creatives and passionate team members. Here, we turn dreams into stardom and audiences into fans. We are guided by three core values that underpin everything we do across all our diverse businesses: 

  • Curiosity: We do our best work when we’re immersing ourselves in culture and breaking through barriers. Curiosity is the driving force behind creativity and ingenuity. It fuels innovation, and innovation is the key to our future. 

  • Collaboration: Making music and bringing it to the world is all about the power of originality amplified by teamwork. A great idea, like a great song, travels globally. We ignite passions and build connections across our diverse community of artists, songwriters, partners, and fans.

  • Commitment: We pursue excellence for our team and our talent. Everything in music starts with a leap into the unknown, and we’re committed to keeping the faith, acting with integrity, and delivering on our promises.

WMG is home to a wide range of artists, musicians, and songwriters that fuel our success. That is why we are committed to creating a work environment that actively values, appreciates, and respects everyone.  We encourage applications from people with a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences.

Consider a career at WMG and get the best of both worlds – an innovative global music company that retains the creative spirit of a nimble independent.
 

At Warner Music Group, we’re a global collective of music makers and music lovers, tech innovators and inspired entrepreneurs, game-changing creatives and passionate team members. Here, we turn dreams into stardom and audiences into fans. We are guided by three core values that underpin everything we do across all our diverse businesses: 

  • Curiosity: We do our best work when we’re immersing ourselves in culture and breaking through barriers. Curiosity is the driving force behind creativity and ingenuity. It fuels innovation, and innovation is the key to our future. 

  • Collaboration: Making music and bringing it to the world is all about the power of originality amplified by teamwork. A great idea, like a great song, travels globally. We ignite passions and build connections across our diverse community of artists, songwriters, partners, and fans.

  • Commitment: We pursue excellence for our team and our talent. Everything in music starts with a leap into the unknown, and we’re committed to keeping the faith, acting with integrity, and delivering on our promises.

WMG is home to a wide range of artists, musicians, and songwriters that fuel our success. That is why we are committed to creating a work environment that actively values, appreciates, and respects everyone.  We encourage applications from people with a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences.

Consider a career at WMG and get the best of both worlds – an innovative global music company that retains the creative spirit of a nimble independent.

Your role:

Reporting to the Senior Director, the Senior Manager of Corporate Finance will play a leadership role on the team responsible for global finance oversight. This is an autonomous, hands-on role where you will oversee controllership across a broad, multi-department portfolio of centrally managed departments while remaining actively involved in the day-to-day execution of month-end close, forecasting, and operational finance tasks. You will collaborate with senior leadership across numerous departments, regional finance leads globally, Corporate Finance, and Regional Offices to drive strategic alignment and financial accountability. 

Here you’ll get to:

  • Fully own the budget across a broad portfolio of centrally managed departments, building an effective forecasting process and ensuring we hit budget by understanding the numbers, identifying risks early, and proactively partnering with senior department heads to implement cost-mitigation or reallocation strategies, not just reporting. 

  • Lead monthly financial close and reporting processes for centrally managed departments, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and alignment with corporate reporting standards. 

  • Lead the consolidated review of centrally managed departments’ P&L—personally building detailed Excel variance models and summaries—while synthesizing complex data into both department-level and consolidated executive-ready summaries of spend vs. budget and progress to targets for senior leadership across multiple departments. 

  • Establish advanced tracking, risk identification, and solution recommendations with enough lead time to act, producing clean, accurate, and actionable financial visibility. 

  • Oversee headcount, payroll, and bonus-related expense reviews, ensuring appropriate accruals, allocations, cost tracking and reporting across an expanded scope of global departments. 

  • Act as a senior finance business partner and strategic advisor to global stakeholders across numerous departments (e.g., A&R, Marketing, Sync, Catalog, Finance/Executive, and other centrally managed functions), providing actionable insights through regular actuals and forecast review discussions. 

  • Facilitate cross-affiliate recharges for central marketing campaigns and funds, as well as maintenance and facilitation of ad-hoc central funding pools. 

  • Remain deeply hands-on with operational finance execution, partnering cross-functionally with Finance SSC and Procurement teams to directly handle and oversee journal entries troubleshooting, PO approvals, invoice coding, and issue resolution, bridging the gap between finance and the wider business. 

  • Own and maintain complex global reporting schedules, including but not limited to department overhead spend performance, M&A legal fee tracking, and SG&A savings initiatives. 

  • Support internal and external audit requirements, including local statutory audit deliverables and documentation readiness. 

  • Drive continuous improvement of reporting processes by enhancing templates, streamlining workflows, and improving forecasting/actuals review efficiency. 

  • Lead and hands-on build the financial modeling and detailed buildup for the annual Budget and 3-Year Plan across a broad portfolio of centrally managed departments, partnering directly with executive leadership to align resources with long-term strategic goals. 

  • Respond to ad-hoc financial reporting requests, providing clear insights and actionable recommendations to business leaders. 

About you: 

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Accounting or Economics – CPA preferred but not required 

  • 8+ years of relevant industry experience with a proven track record of managing complex financial operations and cross-functional partnerships. 

  • An owner mentality, comfortable leading executive-level discussions while remaining deeply willing and able to get into the daily weeds of POs, journal entries, and detailed Excel modeling. 

  • Driver of change and development of ‘best in class’ processes and reporting 

  • High sense of ownership and personal accountability for deliverables and departmental financial performance. 

  • Demonstrated track record of independently managing end-to-end multi-departmental budgets and proactively resolving variance risks without requiring step-by-step oversight. 

  • Excellent analytical, visualization, and storytelling skills—proven ability to translate complex financial data into clear, executive-level presentations, narrative-driven insights, and actionable recommendations for C-suite, senior leadership, and non-finance department heads. 

  • Strong interpersonal skills, demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and effectively influence senior stakeholders across multiple functions. 

  • Advanced Excel proficiency required; strong adaptability and demonstrated success navigating ERPs, financial planning tools (e.g., SAP, Anaplan, or Hyperion), and leveraging AI tools to automate reporting workflows. 

  • Experience within the music industry is a plus 


As the home to 10K Projects, Asylum, Atlantic Music Group, East West, FFRR, Fueled by Ramen, Nonesuch, Parlophone, Rhino, Roadrunner, Sire, Warner Records, Warner Classics, and several other of the world’s premier recording labels, Warner Music Group champions emerging artists and global superstars alike. And our renowned publishing company, Warner Chappell Music, represents genre-spanning songwriters and producers through a catalog of more than one million copyrights worldwide. Warner Music Group is also home to ADA, which supports the independent community, as well as artist services division WMX. In addition, WMG counts film and television storytelling powerhouse Warner Music Entertainment among its many brands.

Together, we are Warner Music Group: Independent Minds. Major Sound.

Click the “Apply” link at the top of the page, or apply directly with your LinkedIn. Applying with LinkedIn will import all of the information you put in your profile, but will still allow you to upload a resume and cover letter.

 

Don’t be discouraged if you don’t hear from us right away. We’re taking our time to review all resumes, and to find the best people for WMG.

 

Thanks for your interest in working for WMG. We love it here, and think you will, too.

This role serves as a technical resource for Viz graphics workflows, ticker systems, L-Bar applications, data integrations, and real-time content delivery while helping ensure reliable operation of critical production systems.

job.title: Director, Event Partnership Strategy & Development
job.description:
The NFL is seeking a Director, Event Partnership Strategy & Development to help drive the growth, innovation, and commercial success of the League's Events & International portfolio. Working closely with senior leadership, this role will lead strategic partnership initiatives, manage critical League commercial relationships, and identify new opportunities to expand revenue, enhance fan engagement, and strengthen the NFL's event platforms. 

The Director will serve as a key connector across Events, International, Sponsorship, Media, Consumer Products, Finance, Corporate Strategy, and the 32 Clubs. The role will develop business strategies, evaluate growth opportunities, and execute high-impact initiatives across major NFL tentpole events, including the Super Bowl, NFL Draft, NFL Scouting Combine, Kickoff, NFL Flag Championships, and International Games. 

The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking, commercial acumen, relationship leadership, analytical rigor, and execution excellence. This individual will be comfortable moving between long-range strategy and day-to-day partner management, translating insights into clear recommendations and measurable business results. 

Responsibilities

Partnership Strategy & Commercial Management 

  • Serve as the day-to-day business lead for select League commercial partnerships, including On Location and event retail partners, managing relationships that drive meaningful revenue, fan engagement, operational performance, and long-term strategic value. 
  • Develop and execute growth plans that maximize commercial performance and identify opportunities to expand assets, activation platforms, audience reach, and partner value. 
  • Establish clear objectives, governance, performance expectations, and issue-escalation paths with partners to ensure consistent delivery against contractual and strategic commitments. 
  • Build trusted relationships with senior executives across partner organizations, serving as a strategic advisor and solution-oriented representative of the League. 
  • Support the development, negotiation, renewal, and implementation of strategic commercial agreements in partnership with Legal, Finance, and other stakeholders. 

Strategic Growth & Business Development 

  • Lead the identification, evaluation, and advancement of new revenue opportunities, business models, partnership structures, and growth initiatives across the NFL's Major Events & International portfolio. 
  • Help shape the long-term business strategy for key NFL event platforms, defining future commercial opportunities, fan experiences, and growth priorities that support broader League objectives. 
  • Develop business cases, strategic frameworks, and executive recommendations to evaluate potential investments, partnerships, new platforms, and other commercial opportunities. 
  • Monitor market trends, consumer behavior, emerging technologies, and competitive activity across sports, entertainment, media, hospitality, and live events to identify opportunities that strengthen the NFL's business position. 

Cross-Functional Leadership & Execution 

  • Lead cross-functional teams through the end-to-end development and execution of strategic initiatives, establishing clear objectives, workplans, decision points, responsibilities, and measures of success. 
  • Collaborate across Events, International, Sponsorship, Finance, Media, Consumer Products, Legal, Club Business Development, and other League functions to develop integrated business solutions and drive alignment. 
  • Oversee concurrent workstreams from concept through implementation, ensuring initiatives are delivered on time, within scope, and in accordance with League priorities and partner commitments. 
  • Anticipate risks, identify challenges and interdependencies, and proactively develop recommendations that support successful execution and sustainable business outcomes. 

Executive Communications & Stakeholder Engagement 

  • Prepare and present business cases, strategic recommendations, partnership updates, and performance assessments for senior leadership, ownership committees, Clubs, and external partners. 
  • Develop post-event and post-initiative assessments that capture business performance, key learnings, growth opportunities, and recommendations for future improvement.  
  • Establish performance measurement frameworks, KPIs, and reporting tools that provide clear visibility into commercial results, partner delivery, and areas for future growth. 
  • Translate complex business issues, research, and financial information into clear insights and actionable recommendations for senior leadership and other decision-makers. 

People & Team Leadership 

  • Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, and development for assigned team members and project resources, setting clear priorities and reinforcing accountability, collaboration, and high-quality execution. 
  • Help allocate resources across partnership management, business development, analytical work, and strategic initiatives to ensure the team remains focused on the highest-impact priorities. 
  • Contribute to a high-performing and inclusive team culture that values commercial curiosity, sound judgment, continuous improvement, and shared success. 

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in business, finance, strategy, or a related field is a plus. 
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in sports, media, entertainment, live events, hospitality, consulting, financial services, or another commercially oriented business environment. 
  • Demonstrated experience developing business cases, partnership strategies, revenue growth initiatives, or new business opportunities. 
  • Strong commercial and financial acumen, including experience evaluating revenue models, forecasts, investments, and performance metrics. 
  • Proven ability to manage complex partner relationships and influence senior internal and external stakeholders without direct authority.

job.title: Director, Paid Social
job.description:
Job Description:


The New York Post provides readers with the best in News, Sports, Pop Culture, Fashion and Entertainment  – with signature wit, irreverence and authority averaging 90 million unique viewers a month. Over the past 225 years, The Post has evolved into a multi-platform media company spanning print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce.

The New York Post is seeking a full-time Director, Paid Social to help lead the paid social strategy and play a pivotal role in growing the business. You will collaborate closely with video, design, marketing, and product teams to ensure a cohesive and engaging experience for our followers.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Social Media, you will have a significant impact on the success of brand partnerships, sponsorship opportunities and paid social across the business. 

Job Responsibilities:

  • Own the paid social strategy across The New York Post's portfolio, serving as the internal subject matter expert across planning, activation, optimization, measurement, and emerging opportunities.

  • Lead and mentor a team of paid social professionals, providing direction and coaching while establishing scalable workflows, processes, and best practices.

  • Develop and execute end-to-end paid social strategies that grow audience, engagement, traffic, content reach, and revenue, while aligning with broader company objectives.

  • Manage and optimize campaigns across Meta (Facebook/Instagram), TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Snapchat, and X, staying ahead of platform updates, new products, and emerging capabilities.

  • Partner with the Senior Director of Social Media, editorial, and social teams to connect paid and organic strategy, identify high-potential content, and drive audience growth and monetization.

  • Collaborate with Sales, Brand Partnerships, marketing, product, design, and video teams to develop cohesive paid-social campaigns, sponsorship solutions, and advertiser programs.

  • Serve as a strategic partner to internal stakeholders, using platform expertise, audience insights, performance data, and reporting to make recommendations and drive optimization.

  • Build and maintain performance dashboards, reporting frameworks, and KPIs while monitoring campaign pacing and identifying opportunities to improve results.

  • Identify and test new platforms, formats, targeting strategies, tools, and optimization techniques, acting as an internal trend spotter across the evolving social ecosystem.

  • Educate stakeholders on paid social capabilities and best practices while balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution in a fast-paced, 24/7 media environment. 

What We’re Looking For: 

  • 4+ years of experience in paid social, paid media, digital media, or a related field, with significant hands-on campaign management and optimization experience.

  • 1–2+ years of experience managing, mentoring, or leading a team.

  • Deep knowledge of paid social platforms, including Meta/Facebook/Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Snapchat, and X.

  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing paid social strategies across planning, activation, optimization, measurement, and reporting.

  • Strong understanding of paid social fundamentals, including audience development, campaign structure, bidding, pacing, budget management, creative formats, targeting, and optimization.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex data into clear insights and actionable recommendations, including experience building dashboards and reporting to senior stakeholders.

  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with experience partnering across editorial, sales, marketing, product, design, video, and social teams.

  • Experience in a publisher, media company, agency, entertainment organization, or other fast-paced digital environment is highly valued, along with an understanding of the relationship between content, audience growth, paid media, and revenue.

job.title: Creative Director
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Deadline: Please submit your application by 5:00 pm EST on Friday, October 2nd, 2026.

Application Instructions

In addition to a resume, please submit:

  • Instead of a traditional cover letter, provide a brief statement outlining your approach to creative leadership, team mentorship, and how you balance artistic innovation with organizational goals.

Intro to Position

NPR is one of the country’s most trusted brands, but its reputation was built in a media landscape that no longer exists. Audiences have scattered across owned platforms, social video, and a dozen competitors fighting for the same attention. The organizations winning that fight are the ones willing to look and sound different, not just distribute more. This role exists to help NPR make that shift real.

This is, and is not, a caretaker role for an established brand. It's a build and evolution role: new formats, new visual language, a creative team stood up for video at a scale the organization hasn't operated in before. 

You'll report to the SVP of Brand & Communications and work closely with Product, Audience Insights, Marketing, and Editorial to shift a beloved legacy brand into one that can compete with new creators and challengers.

Responsibilities

Drive a more distinctive cohesive brand in a saturated market

  • Establish technical brand standards, visual principles, and digital design systems that make NPR’s visual expression instantly recognizable across direct-to-audience platforms. 
  • Build platform-native video formats and visual frameworks that drive industry-leading differentiation, compelling audiences to choose NPR over thousands of alternative journalism and entertainment options 
  • Push beyond generic institutional and media-industry conventions to create work with greater personality, clarity, emotion, and cultural relevance.
  • Translate organizational values, editorial priorities, and public service mission into standardized motion assets, video packages, and platform-native visual frameworks. 
  • Analyze market landscapes and digital competitor trends to ensure NPR’s video and motion visual language remains distinct, modern, and culturally relevant. 

Build creative capacity for an owned-and-operated future

  • Define the technical visual frameworks and motion standards required to integrate video seamlessly across NPR’s owned digital ecosystem (websites, mobile apps, newsletters, and membership portals). 
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Editorial teams to establish a cohesive UI/UX and motion experience across owned platform touchpoints. 
  • Build modular, scalable design systems and template kits that enable teams across the organization to independently publish brand-aligned digital content. 
  • Ensure that creative work supports a deeper direct relationship with audiences rather than treating owned platforms simply as distribution channels.
  • Help develop the visual and verbal conventions that make the organization’s digital experiences feel distinctive, intentional, and connected.
  • Identify opportunities to use design, storytelling, video, motion, and other creative tools to increase engagement with owned experiences.
  • Utilize audience analytics and engagement data to continuously optimize digital assets and direct-to-audience visual experiences. 

Build a modern video and motion capability

  • Establish production standards, camera/lighting guidelines, motion graphic templates, and editing signatures for short-form, social, explanatory, and talent-led video formats. 
  • Procure, maintain, and manage specialized video studio hardware, camera packages, lighting setups, field audio gear, and editing suites 
  • Partner with Editorial and other teams to determine where technical brand video and motion graphics complement editorial production.
  • Develop recognizable approaches to motion, editing, typography, graphics, sound, pacing, and visual storytelling.
  • Ensure that video is treated as a core creative medium rather than an adaptation of work conceived for print or static digital formats.
  • Supervise a dedicated, technical video and motion production squad (2 direct reports), managing daily project allocations, post-production workflows, and technical skill development 

Drive creative excellence

  • Establish operational SLAs, resource management models, and quality-assurance protocols to scale high-volume video publishing efficiently. 
  • Lead the creative development of campaigns, executive communications, fundraising materials, events, presentations, reports, digital experiences, and other strategic initiatives.
  • Ensure creative work is aligned with organizational priorities, audience needs, accessibility standards, and brand guidelines.
  • Encourage experimentation while maintaining consistency and quality.
  • Enforce strict compliance with federal digital accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1, closed captioning, color contrast, screen-reader compatibility) across all motion and video deliverables. 

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 8+ years of progressive creative leadership experience specializing in digital media, video production, or motion systems architecture within an in-house team or agency environment. 
  • Exceptional portfolio demonstrating advanced technical mastery  conceptual thinking, creative direction, visual sophistication, and digital product visual identity across multi-platform ecosystems.
  • Demonstrated experience helping a brand evolve, modernize, or become more differentiated.
  • Deep technical proficiency in industry-standard video and motion software suites (Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, Figma design systems) and the changing ways audiences discover, consume, and engage with media.
  • Meaningful experience developing or directing video and motion work.
  • Demonstrated ability to build relationships, influence cross-functional partners, and navigate complex organizational structures.
  • Experience managing agencies, freelancers, and creative budgets.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with a media, technology, cultural, entertainment, consumer, nonprofit, or mission-driven brand undergoing significant transformation.
  • Experience helping an established or legacy brand evolve for new audiences or platforms.
  • Experience supporting direct-to-consumer, subscription, membership, or other owned-and-operated digital strategies.
  • Experience building or expanding an internal video, motion, or multimedia creative capability.
  • Experience developing enterprise design systems or brand governance frameworks.
  • Familiarity with audience research, brand measurement, accessibility standards, and emerging creative technologies.
  • Demonstrated experience directly managing technical creative personnel, such as video editors, motion designers, and digital production leads. 

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Strong technical storytelling instincts across motion, video, and platform-native digital formats. 
  • Fluency in visual systems, digital motion design, video production workflows, and digital brand expression. 
  • Deep curiosity about media, culture, design technology, motion trends, and changing audience behavior on owned digital platforms.
  • Strong people leadership, technical team management, coaching, and talent-development skills.
  • Comfort leading creative/digital visual transformation within and systems integration within an established organization.
  • An ability to respect the equity of a legacy brand without being constrained by its history when building new platform formats.
  • Excellent collaboration and relationship-building skills across cross functional teams.
  • An ability to communicate the strategic, technical, and architectural reasoning behind creative choices.
  • Comfort navigating ambiguity, organizational complexity, and competing priorities.
  • Strong decision-making and prioritization skills.
  • A commitment to accessibility, inclusion, and creating work for a broad and diverse public.

Education Requirements

  • Equivalent hands-on experience, in lieu of a bachelor’s degree.

Work Location & Requirements

  • NPR Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. The employee will be required to be in the office at the Washington, D.C. or New York City location at least 3 days a week. The employee must also be in commuting distance to Washington, D.C or New York City.

Job Type

job.title: Temporary Video Producer III, Planet Money
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Instructions or Deadline: 

Application Deadline: Monday, October 12th at 5pm ET.

Materials to Submit:

  • A cover letter detailing your creative approach to explanatory journalism on video, your vision for adapting audio reporting to social platforms, and how you foster collaborative learning environments for colleagues new to video production.
  • Links to three short-form videos you conceived, shot, or edited that best illustrate your storytelling technique, editorial judgment, and technical execution. Please provide brief contextual notes on your specific role in each project within your cover letter.

Intro to Position

We’re looking for an experienced video maker to help us transition into a new era of video at Planet Money. The role is part creator, part strategist, part trainer.

Maybe you are a creator ready to join a team. Maybe you are a visual journalist who likes to build systems and start things. Maybe you’ve managed social channels and want to apply that to public media journalism. Maybe something else we haven’t thought of. In any case, here’s the job. 

First, you’ll work with the existing podcast/audio teams at Planet Money and The Indicator to pilot different types of social video or different processes for making them. Then together we will assess what works, what’s worth doing, and what’s not, and you’ll help us update our social video strategy and build sustainable workflows based on what we learn. By the end of your assignment, we hope to have a few new ways to represent our audio journalism on new platforms that our existing staff can sustainably carry on. 

A big part of the job will be helping our audio producers become comfortable creating more video on their own. You’ll help the audio team learn new video tools, analyze metrics and make smart choices about what to adapt to video and what not to. 

There’s wide latitude for experimentation, and an excellent team of creative, smart, fun journalists to collaborate with, including our existing video team. You’ll have lots of support and material to work with, and you’ll be a full part of the Planet Money and Indicator teams, with all the access to the podcast and reporting processes you need to make this work, including collaborating with our existing video colleagues. 

This is a temporary role with a specific mission: help a talented podcast team get a sustainable social video operation up and running and set them up to carry it forward after the assignment ends. There may also be some opportunities to pilot longer-form video, but our first priority is getting short-form systems working well. 

A little background may help you decide if this role is right for you:

Planet Money is like a little economics-themed media outlet within NPR. We explain how economics works and how it affects everyone’s life. We use stories to make the explanations memorable. We do this across media: two podcasts, Planet Money and The Indicator; regular segments on Morning Edition and All Things Considered; two newsletters; a nationally distributed weekend broadcast radio hour with How I Built This; a bestselling book; a board game; and, of course, video.

We’re extremely proud of our video presence, which has gone through several eras, beginning with our T-shirt project in 2013, to a series of live-action shorts in 2019, to a runaway TikTok channel starting in 2020. Now we’re ready to experiment more broadly with how Planet Money and The Indicator show up on video, and how we can do it more consistently and more frequently.

We are not replacing or ending our current short video approach. We couldn’t be more proud of that work! 

Our goal is to build on the excellent social videos our video team is already making. We love what we’re making there, and it works! We want to add more frequent videos that are more closely connected to the reporting we’re doing on the podcast and newsletters. To do that, we need more members of our team participating (maybe on camera and maybe in editing, that’s for you to help us answer). We want to find more opportunities to capture video and new processes that make all of that possible in intelligent, thoughtful and creative ways. Then we will know how to invest in our expanded video future. 

That’s where this role comes in. If you think you can help us build it, please apply.

 

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with: SAG-AFTRA. 

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff is defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.    

Responsibilities

  • Work with Planet Money leadership, video creators and NPR visual and social teams to refine and implement Planet Money’s video strategy, gathering and using audience and performance data to inform decisions. 
  • Lead experimentation with different forms of video journalism, assess results and help determine which approaches Planet Money should focus on. 
  • Collaborate with Planet Money and The Indicator editors, producers and hosts to conceive, produce, shoot, edit and publish video for NPR’s platforms and social media.
  • Train and coach some of our audio producers in video production and visual storytelling, video tools and interpreting performance metrics.
  • Develop short-form social video and other visual projects that extend Planet Money and The Indicator’s journalism to new and existing audiences.
  • Write and edit social video posts, captions, stories and other supporting copy and contribute to community engagement alongside other members of the team.
  • Coordinate production, publication and assessment of programming for visual platforms in collaboration with NPR’s visual and social teams.
  • Establish sustainable video production workflows that the podcast teams can continue on their own. 
  • Maintain NPR editorial and ethical guidelines in all production.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • At least four years of experience regularly making videos regularly in a journalistic, explanatory or comparable editorial setting. Please send us samples. 
  • At least two years of experience managing or creating video for social and digital platforms, with demonstrated experience using audience and performance data to inform editorial or creative decisions. 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of and interest in the topics Planet Money and The Indicator cover
  • Experience managing social media channels for a news or media organization, publisher or other editorial brand.
  • Experience helping journalists or other content creators develop video production and visual storytelling skills.

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Mastery of Adobe Creative Cloud programs related to video, photo and design. (Photoshop, After Effects, Premiere).
  • Advanced skill and experience with video podcasting tools such as Riverside, Descript and comparable platforms. 
  • Strong knowledge of YouTube, TikTok, Instagram and other relevant social media platforms, including experience using platform analytics and data for audience growth. 
  • Strong visual storytelling skills and editorial judgment across short-form and social video.
  • Ability to contribute to and execute a comprehensive, cross-platform video and social strategy.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously and work effectively under tight deadlines.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to coach colleagues with varying levels of video experience.
  • Strong understanding of copyright, journalistic ethics and editorial standards.
  • Demonstrated commitment to increasing audience diversity.
  • Proven ability to communicate clearly and to consistently work well with others and as part of a team, demonstrating at all times respect for the diverse constituencies at NPR and within the public radio system.
  • Must be able to lift video equipment weighing up to 30 pounds.
  • Ability and willingness to work varied shifts as needed.

Education Requirements

  • While we value formal education, especially if you’ve studied the topic areas we cover, we do not believe that any specific degree is needed to perform this job successfully. 

Work Location & Requirements

  • Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. The employee will be required to be in the office at the New York City location at least 3 days a week. The employee must also reside in the New York City area. 

Job Type

  • This is a temporary (6-month) full-time position.

Compensation

Hourly Rate: The U.S.-based anticipated hourly rate for this opportunity is $56.26 per hour. The range displayed reflects the maximum hourly rate NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.
