job.description:
The Houston Chronicle is seeking a Food Reporter to cover Houston’s vibrant and diverse culinary scene in fresh, innovative ways. This reporter will be plugged into restaurant trends, chefs and the people shaping Houston’s food culture. This reporter should be the first to report breaking news, from major restaurant openings and closings to chef moves, ownership changes and industry developments.

The Food Reporter will create journalism that meets audiences wherever they are, particularly on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and other social platforms. This role goes beyond traditional food coverage, combining authoritative reporting with creative storytelling, strong audience instincts and a deep understanding of what makes people want to watch, share, discuss and return for more.

From quick social videos and recurring video series to in-depth stories about Houston’s food scene, this reporter will help define how the Chronicle engages food lovers across the city.

Key responsibilities

  • Be first and best in reporting Houston’s food news, including restaurant openings and closures, chef moves, ownership changes, major hires, expansions and insider developments

  • Build strong sourcing among chefs, restaurateurs, hospitality workers, industry leaders and food enthusiasts

  • Cover restaurant trends, chef profiles, emerging cuisines and the human-centered stories behind the meals, with a focus on what matters to Houston’s diverse communities

  • Use social listening, search trends, audience tools and community engagement to identify food conversations and create coverage that resonates

  • Develop recurring social video series and franchises for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube and other platforms

  • Produce quick reactions, interviews, explainers, behind-the-scenes videos and other social-first storytelling

  • Juggle breaking news with longer features, food guides, trend stories and experimental digital formats

  • Collaborate closely with food editors, visuals, audience strategists and other newsroom teams to bring stories to life and extend their reach

We’re looking for someone who

  • Has at least three years of reporting experience, including at least one year covering food, restaurants, culture, business or a related beat

  • Has a strong understanding of Houston’s restaurant scene, chefs, neighborhoods and culinary culture

  • Has a proven ability to break news quickly, accurately and ethically

  • Is deeply plugged into restaurant and food trends and knows how to spot a story before it becomes widely known

  • Has experience creating social video for platforms such as TikTok and Instagram

  • Is comfortable on camera and capable of developing engaging video series, interviews, explainers and field reports

  • Brings a creative mindset to food coverage and is eager to experiment with formats, visuals and storytelling approaches

  • Can balance breaking news with compelling feature reporting that keeps readers and viewers coming back

About the Houston Chronicle:

The Houston Chronicle, recognized for its Pulitzer Prize-winning journalism, serves its 2.3 million residents with content and marketing solutions across two of Houston’s largest websites — HoustonChronicle.com and Chron.com, along with our magazine, television and newspaper brands.  Our mission is to spark conversations that inspire action to create a better Houston.  All our content and the innovative business solutions we provide invite Houstonians to join conversations about a community we’ve been committed to covering and helping prosper for more than 120 years. The community we all call home.

WHAT WE OFFER:

There has never been a more exciting time to join the Houston Chronicle. Our business is growing and transforming every day.  Advertisers are partnering with us to help them navigate new marketing strategies in today’s increasingly complex digital environment. Simply put, the Houston Chronicle is a media company that uses its rich history and data to deliver the most impactful media campaigns for our customers. We leverage our substantial audience reach, coupled with best in class advertising solutions to keep our customer’s brand in front of the right people at the right time.

 Why are we different? Our people! Our company is diverse and filled with smart, passionate people who want to make a difference in their community, regardless of the role they play in the company. We offer an upbeat and collaborative working environment and expect our people to challenge the norm.

About Hearst Newspapers:

With 2,500 employees across the nation, HNP encompasses a network of 24 daily and 52 weekly publications, including the San Francisco Chronicle, Houston Chronicle, San Antonio Express-News and Albany Times Union, several top digital-only news and lifestyle sites, marketing services businesses, and entertainment businesses such as King Features Syndicate. 

At HNP, we are investing in new and innovative ways to tell stories – growing newsrooms, diversifying tools, evolving platforms – to support the millions of people who trust us each month to help them make decisions, take action and be inspired.  

Be a part of something bigger – your headline awaits.

Recognizing the diverse needs of our candidates, if you are interested in applying for employment and need assistance or an accommodation to use our website or regarding the application process, please contact us by email at hnpemployment@hearst.com.  Please do not use this email address to inquire about the status of applications. We will only respond to inquiries concerning requests for a reasonable accommodation through this email address.

The New York Post provides readers with the best in News, Sports, Pop Culture and Entertainment – with signature wit, irreverence and authority averaging 90 million unique viewers a month. Over the past 225 years, The Post has evolved into a multi-platform media company spanning print, digital, video, audio, app, television and commerce.


The New York Post is looking for a creative, versatile Design Editor (Tuesday-Saturday, 6pm-2am) to join our fast-paced newsroom. If you have a passion for bold visuals, a digital-first mindset, and the skills to turn ideas into eye-catching designs, this role is for you. job.title: Licensing Senior Account Manager
job.description:
About ASCAP

The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) is a membership association of more than one million songwriters, composers and music publishers, and represents some of the world’s most talented music creators. Founded and governed by songwriters, composers and publishers, it is the only performing rights organization in the U.S. that operates on a not-for-profit basis. ASCAP licenses a repertory of over 20 million musical works to hundreds of thousands of businesses that use music, including streaming services, cable television, radio and satellite radio and brick and mortar businesses such as retail stores, hotels, clubs, restaurants and bars. ASCAP collects the licensing fees; identifies, matches and processes trillions of performances every year; and returns nearly 90 cents of every dollar back to its members as royalties. The ASCAP blanket license offers an efficient solution for businesses to legally perform ASCAP music while respecting the right of songwriters and composers to be paid fairly. ASCAP puts music creators first, advocating for their rights and the value of music on Capitol Hill, driving innovation that moves the industry forward, building community and providing the resources and support that creators need to succeed in their careers. Learn more and stay in touch at www.ascap.com, on X and Instagram @ASCAP and on Facebook.

# # #

Job Overview:

The Licensing Senior Account Manager is responsible for driving new business and growing revenue by effectively communicating the need for and the benefits of an ASCAP license agreement to prospective new customers, closing deals with such customers as well as maintaining account relationships and concluding renewal deals with existing customers.

The Licensing Senior Account Manager will communicate and collaborate with the Senior and Associate Directors, SVPs and work cross-functionally with others within the Licensing Department (e.g., Operations, Reactive, Customer Service). Additionally, they will work closely with other departments such as Business and Legal Affairs, Revenue Accounting, Distribution, and Global Technology Solutions.

Areas of Responsibility & Accountability:

  • Identify, assess, and drive licensing efforts by generating and converting leads into both new license prospects and “click-through” licensees
  • Negotiate with select prospective new customers, answering questions, following up and remaining engaged until deal closure
  • Manage select accounts by answering customer queries, resolving issues and pursuing outstanding items
  • Develop, maintain and strengthen relationships among licensee accounts
  • Escalate matters/issues to senior team members when prescribed processes meet impediments and/or when otherwise necessary or appropriate
  • Perform as the backup to the Licensing Business Analyst, gathering and disseminating news and business intelligence to ASCAP leadership when they are not available

Qualifications & Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; music industry studies a plus
  • Ability to work independently with guidance from senior team members
  • A minimum of three years of sales, business development and/or customer service experience, preferably in the music and/or media industry
  • Ability to effectively engage in revenue-generating activities to contribute to ASCAP’s revenue goals
  • Ability to clearly and concisely explain detailed subject matter (i.e. ASCAP and the need/benefits of an ASCAP license) to prospective customers
  • Knowledge of music/copyright, entertainment and technology industries preferred
  • Ability to foresee and stay apprised of new licensing opportunities (i.e. products, services, platforms), particularly those utilizing new/emerging technologies, and the ability to synthesize this information into high-quality formats (emails, reports, PowerPoint) for presentation to senior management
  • Proficiency with Salesforce and/or other CRMs preferred
  • Ability to work cross-functionally on multi-faceted projects
  • Ability to take direction and self-motivate; drive to master core responsibilities and to help a team maximize production and achieve goals
  • Excellent organizational, verbal and written communication skills; professional demeanor; ability to interact effectively with all levels of management and external personnel
  • Excellent attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to meet deadlines under pressure
  • Proven ability to multitask, assess and shift priorities around as needed
  • Ability to work well both individually and on a team while sharing pertinent information, supporting colleagues, and encouraging participation
  • This position requires three days per week in the New York office

Compensation/Benefits:

Besides providing a unique and dynamic work environment, there are a few other reasons you should consider ASCAP in your career planning. We also offer generous benefit options that are comprehensive and provide the flexibility that most employees want and need. These health care and financial plan options include the following:

  • A choice of either network-only provider medical and dental plans or more flexible medical and dental plans where you can see providers in or out-of-network
  • Vision plan that offers both in and out-of-network provider options
  • 401(k) Plan that offers pre-tax, Roth, and an after-tax employee contribution option which includes a company match
  • An additional employer paid discretionary profit share contribution, regardless of your participation in the 401(k) Plan
  • Generous time-off policy
  • Health care and dependent care flexible spending accounts
  • Short-term disability insurance/salary continuation and long-term disability insurance
  • Company provided basic life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance
  • Employee gym discounts at select gyms
  • Commuter benefits
  • Voluntary pet health insurance
  • Voluntary auto and homeowner’s insurance
  • Voluntary employee, spouse, and dependent life insurance options
  • Voluntary ID protection Coverage

The above summary of the current benefits is subject to the terms and conditions of the benefit plan documents. This summary is not complete and is subject to the terms of the underlying plan documents. Please note that ASCAP reserves the right to amend or otherwise revise or terminate, at any time and in its sole discretion, its benefit plans, programs, and policies.

Occasional travel for in-person meetings may be required.

The anticipated base salary range for this position is $80,000 to $87,000 and will be determined on an individualized basis depending on several factors that are unique to each candidate including geographic location (due to differences in the cost of labor), skills, education and prior relevant experience.

job.title: Audience Development Executive
job.description:
The Audience Development Executive grows and deepens the audience for Sony Music's C-POP and J-POP repertoire across Taiwan, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. You will own how fans find our artists, how they move from a first stream to a committed fan, and how we understand and act on what those audiences tell us. 

C-POP and J-POP are two of the fastest-moving parts of our regional business, with releases and campaigns increasingly running across several markets at once and audience behaviour that differs sharply between the two. This role is the connective tissue: setting audience strategy per artist and per release, coordinating rollout across markets, and turning streaming, social and first-party data into decisions the marketing teams can act on. Success looks like measurable audience growth market by market, a healthier conversion from casual listener to superfan, and a release calendar for both repertoires that runs as one regional plan rather than several disconnected ones. 

The role is based in Hong Kong and covers Hong Kong, Taiwan and Southeast Asia (SEA). You will sit within Hong Kong, Taiwan and Southeast Asia (SEA) International Marketing community, reporting to the Director, International Marketing in Hong Kong and working closely with the Head of Creative, Southeast Asia, ensuring regional creative alignment while executing tailored campaigns locally. 

 

What you'll do:

Own audience strategy for C-POP and J-POP repertoire 

  • Develop and deliver audience development plans for priority C-POP and J-POP artists, releases and catalogue across Taiwan, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia, with clear objectives for audience growth, retention and conversion. 
  • Segment and size audiences by market, identifying where an artist is over- or under-indexed and where the realistic growth is, then shape campaign priorities and budget recommendations around that. 
  • Build the discovery-to-superfan funnel for each project: map how listeners enter, what moves them deeper, and where they drop out, and design interventions at each stage. 
  • Own the audience narrative for both repertoires in regional planning sessions, bringing a clear point of view backed by data to marketing, creative, commercial and repertoire centre stakeholders. 
  • Recognise where C-POP and J-POP audiences behave differently, in discovery route, fandom structure, spending patterns and platform preference, and build strategies that reflect those differences rather than applying one regional template to both. 

Grow audiences on DSPs and across the streaming ecosystem 

  • Work with digital service partners including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, LINE MUSIC, JOOX, KKBOX and regional platforms on pitching, editorial support, on-platform programming and audience-growth opportunities across both repertoires. 
  • Drive playlist strategy across owned, editorial and algorithmic surfaces, including Filtr and other in-house playlist brands, and track how placement translates into sustained audience rather than a single-week spike. 
  • Partner with the digital marketing and media buying teams to align paid audience targeting with organic audience strategy, so spend is directed where it compounds. 
  • Monitor the creator and short-form ecosystem, identifying tracks and moments gaining traction and working with creative and digital teams to amplify them quickly. 
  • Track and act on the discovery routes specific to J-POP in this region, including anime, film and game sync, tour and event moments, and catalogue resurgence, and convert those spikes into retained audience. 

Build first-party data and superfan capability 

  • Grow first-party data capture across C-POP and J-POP campaigns, working with local teams to embed sign-up and data collection into releases, tours, fan events and D2C moments. 
  • Turn first-party data into usable audience segments for CRM, direct-to-consumer and superfan activity, and support markets in activating those segments responsibly. 
  • Identify and develop superfan opportunities that deepen the relationship with the most engaged part of each artist's audience, and support the commercial cases that sit behind them. 
  • Partner with Sony Music Japan and Greater China repertoire centre teams on first-party data and superfan initiatives, feeding regional audience insight back to them and translating their priorities into market-level plans. 
  • Work within local data protection and privacy requirements across each market, in partnership with legal and the relevant local teams. 

Coordinate across markets and repertoire centres 

  • Act as the regional coordination point for C-POP and J-POP releases and activities, aligning timelines, asset delivery and campaign moments across Taiwan, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. 
  • Consolidate requirements from local marketing teams into workable regional plans that scale while still allowing for hyper-local adaptation. 
  • Maintain visibility of the release calendar and audience plans across both repertoires so markets and the repertoire centres know what is coming and what is expected of them. 
  • Flag risks, clashes and gaps early, and keep regional stakeholders informed of progress and performance. 

Measure, report and improve 

  • Track and report on audience KPIs including listener growth, retention, market share, playlist performance, and first-party data capture, and communicate results clearly to senior stakeholders. 
  • Lead post-campaign reviews, identifying what drove audience growth and feeding those learnings into the next cycle. 
  • Work with the insights, data and analytics team to develop reporting that markets will actually use, and build data literacy across the regional teams. 
  • Stay ahead of platform, format and consumption changes across Greater China and Southeast Asia, and advise the business on what they mean for how we grow audiences.

 

Who you are:

  • 2+ years' experience in audience development, digital marketing, streaming or artist marketing at a label, DSP, artist management company or comparable media business. 
  • Demonstrable track record of growing an artist, catalogue or content audience, with the numbers to show it. 
  • Strong working knowledge of the streaming landscape across Greater China and Southeast Asia, including DSP editorial and algorithmic mechanics, playlist strategy, and platform-specific audience behaviour. 
  • Genuine fluency in C-POP and J-POP: the artists, the fandoms, the platforms they live on, and how audience behaviour differs between Taiwan, Hong Kong and the Southeast Asian markets. 
  • Comfortable with data. Able to work with streaming, social and first-party data, draw a defensible conclusion from it, and explain that conclusion to people who are not analysts. 
  • Experience with first-party data capture, CRM or direct-to-consumer fan initiatives is a strong advantage. 
  • Fluent in Mandarin (Traditional Chinese) and English. Japanese is a strong advantage given the J-POP scope, and Cantonese an advantage given the Hong Kong scope. 
  • Strong coordination skills across multiple markets, time zones and stakeholders, with the ability to keep several campaigns moving at once. 
  • Ability to articulate an idea or point of view succinctly, with clarity and confidence, adapting the message to different audiences, seniority levels and cultures. 
  • Responds and adapts quickly to change, maintaining a flexible attitude and using new conditions to evolve their thinking. 
  • A thorough understanding of lifestyle and cultural trends across Greater China and Southeast Asia.

 

What we give you:

  • You join a vibrant global community with the opportunity to channel your passion every day
  • A modern office environment designed for you, empowering you to bring your best
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt and create what happens next
  • We give you the platform to champion positive change, with the opportunity to contribute to our social impact, diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives

job.title: Marketing Manager
job.description:
As Marketing Manager within Sony Music Entertainment Thailand, you will be the project lead on your assigned roster of domestic artists, responsible for building campaign plans in line with the artists vision and Sony Music.

Within the role you will be working closely with the artists, guiding them on social media, marketing planning and executing marketing and paid advertising strategies for the project, as well as commissioning creative and the marketing tools needed.

You will report to the Senior Marketing Manager of Sony Music Thailand and be joining a passionate group of like-minded and collaborative music fanatics.

What you'll do:

  • Driving end-to-end marketing strategy across all projects. Own the full campaign lifecycle for assigned releases: positioning, audience definition, channel strategy, launch planning, and post-campaign analysis.
  • Leading the team with clear direction, planning, and accountability. Set campaign standards (brief quality, approvals, asset readiness, measurement approach) and keep the team aligned through structured check-ins and progress tracking.
  • Develop creative and audience-centric campaign concepts tailored to each artist’s identity, local culture, and fan behaviours.
  • Elevating campaign quality and creative output to stay competitive. Monitor and interpret platform performance signals (content performance, audience response, and campaign outcomes) to optimize in-flight and future campaigns.
  • Strengthening digital performance through data-driven execution
  • Ensuring scalability as our release volume continues to grow
  • Design audience growth plans that expand beyond core fans—balancing acquisition, engagement, retention, and conversion objectives for each release cycle.
  • Develop creative and audience centric marketing campaigns for your roster of artists.
  • Create and build all local marketing tools, including artist imagery, press images, release artwork, advertising assets and videos
  • Deliver on Artist DNAs, Marketing Plans, and artist updates for all assigned artists. These will outline core marketing objectives that drive streaming, sales, fan acquisition and revenue.
  • Building an artist brand, core pillars and identity in line with the artist vision and Sony Music
  • Forecast project-based marketing and sales budgets
  • Be the day-to-day point person for artist team, Label partner or management on your roster of artists

Who you are:

  • Solid experience running multi-faceted and innovative marketing campaigns, with particular focus on content marketing, artist development and audience growth.
  • Strong creative skills to craft compelling content and messaging that reflects the artist identity, and brand and engages their audience.
  • The ability to thrive in a fast-paced and ever-changing digital environment. Being open to learning new technologies, industry trends, and adjusting strategies accordingly.

Wir suchen kurzfristig einen erfahrenen Finanzbuchhalter

In enger Abstimmung mit dem europäischen Management und der globalen Finance-Organisation stellst du sicher, dass Abschlüsse, Reporting, Compliance und interne Kontrollen verlässlich, fristgerecht und nach einheitlichen Standards umgesetzt werden.

Aufgaben

  • Eigenständige Betreuung der Debitoren- und Kreditorenbuchhaltung
  • Prüfung von Rechnungen und Abwicklung des Zahlungsverkehrs
  • Forderungsmanagement
  • Erstellung der Umsatzsteuermeldungen in allen europäischen Ländern in Zusammenarbeit mit unserem internationalen Compliance Partner

job.title: Sr. Manager, eCommerce Store Operations
job.description:
At Warner Music Group, we’re a global collective of music makers and music lovers, tech innovators and inspired entrepreneurs, game-changing creatives and passionate team members. Here, we turn dreams into stardom and audiences into fans. We are guided by three core values that underpin everything we do across all our diverse businesses: 

  • Curiosity: We do our best work when we’re immersing ourselves in culture and breaking through barriers. Curiosity is the driving force behind creativity and ingenuity. It fuels innovation, and innovation is the key to our future. 

  • Collaboration: Making music and bringing it to the world is all about the power of originality amplified by teamwork. A great idea, like a great song, travels globally. We ignite passions and build connections across our diverse community of artists, songwriters, partners, and fans.

  • Commitment: We pursue excellence for our team and our talent. Everything in music starts with a leap into the unknown, and we’re committed to keeping the faith, acting with integrity, and delivering on our promises.

WMG is home to a wide range of artists, musicians, and songwriters that fuel our success. That is why we are committed to creating a work environment that actively values, appreciates, and respects everyone.  We encourage applications from people with a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences.

Consider a career at WMG and get the best of both worlds – an innovative global music company that retains the creative spirit of a nimble independent.
 

A little bit about our team:

WMX, Warner Music Group’s culture-driving media, creative content, and artist services’ division, sets a new standard for artists, advertisers, and fans through world class experiences, award-winning creative content, and industry leading audience insights. At WMX (Warner Music Experience) we’re building the music industry’s most dynamic artist and fan-centric organization, creating fans and influencing culture through engaging content and best-in-class experiences. We partner with acclaimed brands and emerging artists to create innovative, authentic, world-class consumer experiences.


Ecommerce and Commerce Channels has grown to be a thriving business for artists and brands. Our team partners with artists, labels and executives to develop engaging artist stores, social activations, sales channel extensions and memorable customer experiences.  We develop best in class tools and processes to help internal teams efficiently deliver products and services to fans around the world.


Your role:

We're looking for a Sr. Manager, eCommerce Store Operations to lead a small team of local operations managers.   This role will manage the set up and publishing banners, promotions  and high visibility product launches on our artists stores.   The role is instrumental in helping build fan to artists relationships through product launches and promotional activations.   As part of the global D2C Operations Leadership team you will be instrumental in defining and streamlining business processes and driving outcomes.


Working closely with ecommerce operations, merchandising, marketing, analytics, label / artist teams and technology  partners, you'll support the continued growth and investment in a global eCommerce business that serves hundreds of artists and millions of fans. 


Here you’ll get to:

  • Help own the business process to manage intake requests, allocate resources, execute  and  launch product, promotion and marketing requests on our ecommerce sites. 
  • Manage a direct team of store and item operations managers who operate our customer facing artists stores.
  • Define requirements, and success metrics for our streamlined operations process and drive continuous improvement in team performance. 
  • Own requirements and implementation of project management tools for your area of accountability.  Familiarity with ASANA, AirTable, Monday or JIRA. 
  • Execute visual merchandising strategies to showcase new releases, featured products and promotions effectively and continuously refine presentations to drive improvements in engagement and conversion rates.
  • Collaborate with the store managers / brand management team to understand the goals, objectives, and messaging for new releases, campaigns, and promotions.
  • Execute the timed launch of the campaign according to the predetermined plan and schedule, ensuring all elements are activated accurately.
  • Continuously monitor and track weekly sales on new album releases to ensure chart numbers are accurate while identifying any sales discrepancies.
  • Partner with technology and platform teams to identify and prioritize improvements in business tools, analytics and project management suites to improve business performance. 
  • Coordinate with Customer Service teams to update stores to respond to customer feedback, address issues promptly to minimize exposure.

About you:

  • 5  years of eCommerce and Site Merchandising or store operations experience 
  • Experience supporting product and marketing  campaigns on high visibility stores.
  • Experience working with Shopify or similar eCommerce platforms 
  • Understanding of product catalogs, content management, digital publishing and merchandising processes. 
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally with marketing, merchandising, brand management, customer services and external stakeholders to coordinate product launches. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with stakeholders at all levels
  • Passion for the customer experience and exception service to clients protecting their brand and reputation as well as advocating for a best in class customer experience.
  • Detail oriented and accountable to  quality of overall outcomes and individual teams deliverables. 

We’d love it if you also had:

  • Comfortable using data to prioritize  decisions and measure business impact 
  • Ability to influence and lead indirect reports and peers.
  • Experience  managing cross-functional teams in an agile or kanban environment
  • Experience managing multiple brands storefronts including multiple daily product releases.
  • Bachelor’s Degree preferred


As the home to 10K Projects, Asylum, Atlantic Music Group, East West, FFRR, Fueled by Ramen, Nonesuch, Parlophone, Rhino, Roadrunner, Sire, Warner Records, Warner Classics, and several other of the world’s premier recording labels, Warner Music Group champions emerging artists and global superstars alike. And our renowned publishing company, Warner Chappell Music, represents genre-spanning songwriters and producers through a catalog of more than one million copyrights worldwide. Warner Music Group is also home to ADA, which supports the independent community, as well as artist services division WMX. In addition, WMG counts film and television storytelling powerhouse Warner Music Entertainment among its many brands.

Together, we are Warner Music Group: Independent Minds. Major Sound.

Love this job and want to apply?

Click the “Apply” link at the top of the page, or apply directly with your LinkedIn. Applying with LinkedIn will import all of the information you put in your profile, but will still allow you to upload a resume and cover letter.

 

Don’t be discouraged if you don’t hear from us right away. We’re taking our time to review all resumes, and to find the best people for WMG.

 

Thanks for your interest in working for WMG. We love it here, and think you will, too.
 

This position requires a minimum of 4 days per week in the office. We value in-office collaboration, which is essential for talent development and strong working relationships. #LI-Onsite Salary Range: $80,000 to $90,000 Annually Salary ranges are included for job postings where required by law. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as work experience and business needs. The pay range is subject to change at any time dependent on a variety of internal and external factors.

job.title: AV Technical Event Producer
job.description:
Role: AV Technical Event Producer

Mode: Onsite

Location, Chicago, IL 60602


One of Astreya’s key clients is looking for an experienced, enthusiastic, and organized Technical Event Producer to provide event support and manage and operate Audio/Visual systems at their downtown Chicago office. Event locations include corporate auditoriums, boardrooms, and conference centers. This role reports to the Senior Video & Media Production Manager and supports virtual, in-person, hybrid, and live stream events.


Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with Vendors, Marketing, Sales, Corporate Communications, Talent & Culture, and Infrastructure to manage production needs for in-person, virtual, and live stream events.
  • Work with internal stakeholders regarding event and presentation logistics, production management, and executional delivery.
  • Lead technical and AV crews as well as act as show producer and show caller/director.
  • Project manage and track tasks and deadlines ahead of in-person and remote events and town halls.
  • Project management of: Virtual platforms, technical speaker support, scripts, production schedules, and show flows. Once on-site: assist with AV equipment and staging.
  • Assist in the creation of unique and distinct corporate events and town halls.
  • Work closely with the Lead Technical Producer to coordinate technical logistics and hire subcontractors when needed.
  • Along with the Lead Technical Producer, act as the main stakeholder points of contact for all audio and video production related needs for events
  • Collaborate and communicate with internal stakeholders to ensure alignment and execution of event deliverables.
  • Help create systems to be used in corporate and external spaces not outfitted with AV broadcast systems.
  • Assist with presenter preparation and guidance for successful show execution, when needed.


Qualifications & Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience managing audio/video needs for events and meetings; a focus on corporate events preferred.
  • 3+ years of experience successfully producing, developing, managing, and executing the technical production elements of in-person, remote, and live stream events.
  • Industry knowledge of current production best practices, equipment, and rental costs
  • Domestic and international travel and work across time zones may be required.


Experienced with:

  • vMix Video Switching/Streaming
  • NDI Video
  • Digital Audio Mixer Routing and Operation
  • Zoom Webinars and Meetings
  • Live Sound Reinforcement
  • Creating Show Flows and Runs of Show
  • Shure Wireless Systems


Familiar with:

  • Dante Audio over IP
  • Bitfocus Companion
  • DMX Lighting Operation
  • RTMP Streaming


Core Responsibilities:


Core Responsibilities of an Event Technical Producer

1. Pre-Production / Planning

  • Technical Requirements Gathering
  • Meet with stakeholders to understand creative vision, format (live/virtual/hybrid), and tech needs.
  • Assess venue capabilities or virtual platform requirements.
  • Vendor & Equipment Coordination
  • Source and manage AV, lighting, staging, IT/networking, and streaming vendors.
  • Specify technical equipment (cameras, projectors, mixers, mics, encoders, etc.).
  • Ensure redundancy plans for power, network, and key systems.
  • Site Visits & Network Testing
  • Conduct site surveys to assess power, rigging, sound, Wi-Fi, and video infrastructure.
  • Coordinate with venue IT to confirm bandwidth and IP requirements.
  • Run-of-Show / Technical Script Creation
  • Develop cue sheets, transition plans, and presenter tech instructions.
  • Coordinate load-in/load-out timelines with all vendors and internal teams.


2. Rehearsals & Setup

  • Tech Rehearsals
  • Schedule and lead dry runs with presenters and technical crew.
  • Train speakers on mics, teleprompters, clickers, and virtual tools (e.g., Zoom, Teams, Webex).
  • Equipment Testing & Setup
  • Oversee AV and lighting setup, camera placements, cabling, and show control systems.
  • Test all presentations, videos, click paths, and backup systems.


3. Live Event Execution

  • Production Command
  • Call cues for media playback, speaker transitions, lighting/sound changes.
  • Manage the control room or virtual production desk (Zoom, vMix, BlackMagic, etc.).
  • Troubleshoot real-time issues: mic feedback, frozen video feeds, connectivity drops.
  • Crew Management
  • Direct audio engineers, camera operators, streaming technicians, and stagehands.
  • Ensure everyone adheres to timing and technical flow.
  • Virtual Audience Support (if hybrid/virtual)
  • Monitor streaming platform health and participant experience.
  • Coordinate breakout rooms, polls, Q&A, and platform moderation.


4. Post-Event Wrap-Up

  • Strike & Equipment Return
  • Supervise teardown of equipment and loading out of gear.
  • Ensure rented gear is returned, internal assets are accounted for.
  • Technical Postmortem
  • Debrief with crew and stakeholders: what went well, what needs improvement.
  • Document lessons learned and update templates or procedures.
  • Media Management
  • Ensure recordings are archived, edited, and shared appropriately.
  • Back up assets to storage or shared drives.
  • Budget Reconciliation
  • Track final vendor costs, submit invoices, and align with event producer on reconciliations.


5. Strategic Collaboration on AV Standards

  • The Technical Producer works closely with the AV Engineering team to help define and evolve scalable AV production standards across new and existing office locations—particularly in the design of town hall and all-hands spaces. This includes advising on equipment selection, control systems, camera placement, and acoustics to ensure consistency in production quality and supportability.
  • By bringing live event execution experience into the planning process, the Technical Producer helps shape spaces that are not only technically sound but also operationally efficient for high-impact, repeatable events.

job.title: Senior Director, Brand Marketing
job.description:
Who We Are:

SiriusXM

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, and the premier programmer and platform for subscription and digital advertising-supported audio products. SiriusXM’s platforms collectively reach approximately 150 million listeners, the largest digital audio audience across paid and free tiers in North America, and deliver music, sports, talk, news, comedy, entertainment and podcasts. Pandora, a subsidiary of SiriusXM, is the largest ad-supported audio entertainment streaming service in the U.S. SiriusXM's subsidiaries Stitcher, Simplecast and AdsWizz make it a leader in podcast hosting, production, distribution, analytics and monetization. The Company’s advertising sales organization, which operates as SXM Media, leverages its scale, cross-platform sales organization and ad tech capabilities to deliver results for audio creators and advertisers. SiriusXM, through Sirius XM Canada Holdings, Inc., also offers satellite radio and audio entertainment in Canada. In addition to its audio entertainment businesses, SiriusXM offers connected vehicle services to automakers.


How you’ll make an impact:

We are seeking a strategic thought leader and results-driven Senior Director of Brand Marketing to lead the evolution of the SiriusXM brand. In this high-impact role, you will define how our brand shows up in the world, how it drives emotional connection, cultural relevance, and long-term subscriber growth. You will oversee brand strategy, 360° integrated marketing campaigns, creative execution, and media planning across all consumer touchpoints. Leading a talented, high-performing team, you will bridge the gap between best-in-class brand creative and rigorous, data-driven performance. You will lead the Brand Marketing sub-function across multiple teams, setting long-range priorities and aligning department objectives to functional strategy. You will partner with senior and executive leadership on critical brand decisions with multi-year impact across the company.


What you’ll do:

The ideal candidate is equal parts – Brand Strategist, Marketer, channel planner and analyst.


They will be responsible for supporting all efforts across brand marketing, including:


Brand Strategy & Stewardship

  • Evolve and scale SiriusXM’s brand identity, positioning, and messaging architecture across all consumer touchpoints.
  • Conduct ongoing market, competitive, and consumer research to identify insights that shape impactful brand strategies.
  • Author high-impact strategy decks and business cases to clearly communicate brand direction, launch plans, and ROI to leadership and internal stakeholders.
  • Ensure absolute consistency in brand voice, visual identity, and values across every department.
  • Set a multi-year Brand Marketing strategy and translate functional priorities into objectives, policies, and operating plans for multiple teams.
  • Develop and authorize brand governance standards and implementation practices that guide how the brand is expressed across the organization.

Creative Direction & Campaigns

  • Oversee the ideation, production, and execution of breakthrough, multi-channel brand campaigns across paid, owned and earned.
  • Champion creative excellence, pushing boundaries to create memorable, cultural, and industry-defining work.
  • Direct investment priorities across brand campaigns, agencies, production, and media; ensure budgets and schedules meet corporate requirements.

Leadership & Team Growth

  • Lead and develop the Brand Marketing organization through managers and senior managers with accountability for multiple teams and areas of work.
  • Foster a collaborative, high-performance culture that values new ideas, creative experimentation, and accountability.
  • Devote time to developing future leaders, strengthening succession readiness, and coaching managers to build high-performing teams.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with programming, events, dealership and business teams to seamlessly integrate brand narrative into performance campaigns, product launches, and audience funnels.
  • Collaborate with Internal Communications and HR to ensure the employer brand aligns authentically with the external corporate brand.
  • Influence senior and executive leaders on critical brand matters, gaining alignment on long-range priorities, policies, and cross-functional decisions.

Measurement & Analytics

  • Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for brand health, including brand awareness, consideration and listening metrics.
  • Translate brand data and performance metrics into actionable insights for leadership and cross functional partners.
  • Use brand, consumer, competitive, and business signals to anticipate emerging issues and set frameworks for decisions with long-term impact.

What you’ll need:

  • Bachelor's degree with focus on marketing or related field, or equivalent, relevant experience.
  • Typically has 12 or more years of experience with 6 or more years of management experience.
  • Leadership Skills: You’re a people manager who has experience leading teams. You’re someone that has a clear vision and strategy for your org. You know how to effectively communicate department goals to your team, as well as motivate and support your people in meeting those objectives. You always put your people first – you listen, inspire and coach.
  • Entrepreneurial: You’re a self-starter who gets excited at the chance to run initiatives end-to-end with full ownership and autonomy. You have no problem getting down in the weeds but can also pivot to be strategic and provide thought leadership support.
  • Results-Oriented: You are someone that drives outcomes with a demonstrated track record for improving results in business performance. You take a focused approach towards action and rapid testing. You know how to extract learnings from both wins and losses.
  • Analytical & Intensely Curious: You have a strong aptitude for data and reporting. You are familiar with and embrace tools of the trade including Tableau or similar BI platforms (i.e. Adobe reporting, Google Analytics, etc.). You are constantly analyzing all available data. You’re always building a roadmap of hypotheses and experiments to test to improve results for the business.
  • You’re a Facilitator: You are acutely aware of all the moving pieces necessary to build campaigns and can collaborate with other groups to execute.
  • You have a creative streak: A keen eye for top performing creative and the ability to work with multiple stakeholders and design and copywriting teams to develop best in class creative executions.
  • Exhibit strong verbal and written communication skills, public speaking, presentation skills and excellent interpersonal skills.
  • Demonstrate excellent attention to detail, time management skills, and an ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a highly fluid, fast-paced environment.
  • Thorough knowledge of MS-Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook).
  • Must have legal right to work in the U.S.

At SiriusXM, we carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including your background and experience. These considerations can cause your compensation to vary. We expect the base salary for this position to be in the range of $146,600 to $202,800 and will depend on your skills, qualifications, and experience. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary short-term and long-term incentives. We encourage all interested candidates to apply.


Our goal at SiriusXM is to provide and maintain a work environment that fosters mutual respect, professionalism and cooperation. SiriusXM is an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate on the basis of actual or perceived race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, alienage or citizenship status, age, disability or handicap, sex, gender identity, marital status, familial status, veteran status, sexual orientation or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.


The requirements and duties described above may be modified or waived by the Company in its sole discretion without notice.

job.title: Director, Content Marketing
job.description:
Who We Are:

SiriusXM and its brands (Pandora, SiriusXM Media, AdsWizz, Simplecast, and SiriusXM Connect) are leading a new era of audio entertainment and services by delivering the most compelling subscription and ad-supported audio entertainment experience for listeners -- in the car, at home, and anywhere on the go with connected devices. Our vision is to shape the future of audio, where everyone can be effortlessly connected to the voices, stories and music they love wherever they are.


This is the place where a diverse group of emerging talent and legends alike come to share authentic and purposeful songs, stories, sounds and insights through some of the best programming and technology in the world. Our critically-acclaimed, industry-leading audio entertainment encompasses music, sports, comedy, news, talk, live events, and podcasting. No matter their individual role, each of our employees plays a vital part in bringing SiriusXM’s vision to life every day.


SiriusXM:

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, and the premier programmer and platform for subscription and digital advertising-supported audio products. SiriusXM’s platforms collectively reach approximately 150 million listeners, the largest digital audio audience across paid and free tiers in North America, and deliver music, sports, talk, news, comedy, entertainment and podcasts. Pandora, a subsidiary of SiriusXM, is the largest ad-supported audio entertainment streaming service in the U.S. SiriusXM's subsidiaries Simplecast and AdsWizz make it a leader in podcast hosting, production, distribution, analytics and monetization. The Company’s advertising sales organization, which operates as SiriusXM Media, leverages its scale, cross-platform sales organization and ad tech capabilities to deliver results for audio creators and advertisers. SiriusXM, through SiriusXM Canada Holdings, Inc., also offers satellite radio and audio entertainment in Canada. In addition to its audio entertainment businesses, SiriusXM offers connected vehicle services to automakers.


How you’ll make an impact:

SiriusXM is seeking a strategic, creative, and data-driven Director, Content Marketing to lead the development and execution of multi-channel content marketing campaigns that drive subscriber acquisition, deepen listener engagement and strengthen brand affinity.  


This role will oversee content marketing across paid, owned, and earned media for both SiriusXM and Pandora. From promoting exclusive artist channels and major sports seasons to launching hit podcasts and celebrity talk shows, you will ensure our content shines across all consumer touchpoints.


The ideal candidate is a modern content leader who understands how to build integrated campaigns, manage editorial calendars, lead cross-functional teams, and turn audience insights into breakthrough creative. The Director of Content Marketing will partner closely with Brand Marketing, Growth Marketing, Programming, Talent Relations, Social, PR, Product Marketing, Creative, CRM, Partnerships, and Analytics teams to ensure SiriusXM shows up with consistent, engaging, and measurable content across the listener journey.


What you'll do:


Content Strategy & Leadership:

  • Develop and lead content marketing strategies across SiriusXM and Pandora, programming categories, tentpole campaigns, talent partnerships, cultural moments and audience-growth initiatives.
  • Create integrated content plans that support brand awareness, listener engagement, subscriber acquisition, retention, win-back, and cross-platform discovery.
  • Translate programming priorities into marketable stories, campaign themes, editorial packages, social-first concepts, landing page content, video franchises, short-form copy, and partner-ready messaging.
  • Own and manage a cross-channel content calendar that aligns marketing, programming, social, PR, CRM, product, and partnership priorities.
  • Lead the Content Marketing function as a department-level leader, setting strategic priorities, operating plans, resource allocation, and measurable objectives in alignment with broader Marketing and company goals.
  • Participate with senior management in establishing content marketing strategy and priorities, and provide recommendations on initiatives with meaningful impact on audience growth, engagement, acquisition, retention, and brand outcomes.

Campaign Development & Execution:

  • Lead the content strategy for major campaigns tied to SiriusXM and Pandora programming, exclusive channels, artist moments, sports seasons, comedy specials, talk programming, live events, podcasts, and seasonal initiatives.
  • Partner with Creative and Brand teams to develop campaign concepts, copy platforms, video/storytelling ideas, and audience-specific content assets.
  • Collaborate with Growth, Lifecycle, and CRM teams to create content that moves listeners from discovery to trial, conversion, engagement, renewal, and advocacy.
  • Support partnership marketing efforts by developing content packages and co-marketing narratives for talent, media partners, advertisers, automotive partners, device partners, and distribution platforms.
  • Exercise primary decision-making authority for content marketing priorities, campaign sequencing, channel and asset recommendations, and resource tradeoffs within the function, while escalating enterprise-level decisions as appropriate.

Audience, Performance & Insights:

  • Use audience research, behavioral data, search trends, social listening, content performance, and campaign analytics to inform content strategy and optimization.
  • Define KPIs for content marketing initiatives, including engagement, reach, conversion, retention, content consumption, click-through rate, subscriber impact, and campaign lift.
  • Lead regular performance reporting, turning insights into clear recommendations for future creative, channel strategy, programming support, and audience targeting.
  • Establish multi-year content marketing capabilities, measurement practices, and operating improvements that strengthen the function's effectiveness and scale.

Cross-Functional Collaboration:

  • Serve as a senior content marketing partner to Programming, Product, Brand, Growth, Social, PR, Partnerships, CRM, Sales Marketing, and Analytics teams.
  • Lead cross-functional planning sessions to align campaign goals, audience priorities, messaging, asset needs, timelines, and distribution strategies.
  • Manage stakeholders through complex campaign development, balancing creative ambition, business objectives, legal requirements, talent approvals, and production timelines.
  • Partner with internal and external creative resources, agencies, freelancers, producers, writers, designers, editors, and video teams as needed.
  • Regularly influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners on content marketing priorities, investment choices, operating tradeoffs, and initiatives significant to the organization.

Team & Operational Leadership:

  • Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing content marketing team, fostering a culture of creativity, accountability, collaboration, and measurable impact.
  • Create scalable processes for intake, prioritization, editorial planning, content development, approvals, asset delivery, reporting, and post-campaign learning.
  • Manage budgets, agency scopes, freelance resources, production timelines, and content operations with discipline and transparency.
  • Stay ahead of trends in audio, streaming, music, podcasts, sports media, creator marketing, entertainment marketing, short-form video and audience development.
  • Direct and develop people managers and/or teams within Content Marketing, with accountability for staffing, performance management, coaching, succession planning, and development of future leaders.
  • Own annual planning and budget priorities for the Content Marketing function, including staffing, agency and freelance investment, production resources, and expense tradeoffs.

What you’ll need:

  • Typically has 10+ years of experience within a content marketing and/or digital marketing function, preferably within digital, Mobile and/or email channel. 
  • 5+ years of leadership experience managing teams.

Beijing has leveraged its might, both commercially and militarily, to redraw the terms of trade, security and diplomacy. Under Xi Jinping’s leadership, China has sought to offer a model of governance that challenges the liberal democratic order and the dominance of the United States.

It touches nearly every major issue. Geopolitics. Demographics. Inequality. Climate Change. Trade. Technology. 

The role requires a strong writer with the ability to juggle breaking news, smart analysis and ambitious enterprise. We want someone eager to react quickly to news as necessary, but who is also able to write thoughtfully and deeply about important issues and events. We are looking for an entrepreneurial correspondent who can embrace the multitudes, to cover the news and the nuance.

job.title: Correspondent, The Economics of a Warming World
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Climate change is reshaping insurance markets, agriculture, supply chains, labor productivity, real estate, facility planning and the flow of capital and trade globally. It is a central force reordering how industries make decisions and compelling societies to make difficult choices about how to spend scarce resources. It is pulsing through economies, but often goes unrecognized. 

We’re creating a new beat to fix that.

This correspondent will reveal the economic implications of a warming planet. It’s one of the most significant coverage areas in the world today, touching on energy and trade, shifting global economic alliances and the complex calculations being made by societies that may determine prosperity or poverty for generations.

The mandate spans everything from why insurers are pulling out of entire states, to how ports are redesigning for rising seas, to how central banks are beginning to price climate risk into monetary policy and ways that a warming world is forcing governments to spend more.

This correspondent will also have the investigative skills to reveal which entities are profiting from a changing climate and how they use power and money to their advantage, influencing markets and government policies.  

This is a rare opportunity to define a beat from scratch.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in a NYT office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities: 

  • Report ahead of the curve and break news — Curiosity that leads you to  identify which industries, regions, or asset classes are about to face a climate reckoning before it becomes obvious to the public or even to the industries themselves. We want stories nobody else has found
  • Write standout features that use narratives and data to make abstract risk tangible: the Iowa farmer recalibrating for a new growing season, the Miami condo board fighting over special assessments, the highway engineer redesigning for freeze-thaw cycles that no longer freeze. 
  • Illuminate how climate risk is moving through the economy: insurance repricing, credit downgrades, corporate disclosures, agricultural futures, real estate valuations and municipal bond markets and write about it in an engaging, accessible way
  • Translate science into economic consequences — fluently connecting climate models, weather data, and physical risk research to markets, prices, and policy with graceful language that leads readers to say ”Now I understand!”
  • Build a network of sources across insurance, agriculture, utilities, construction, banking, and academia 
  • Collaborate with Business, Real Estate, National, Weather and other desks to produce ambitious work
  • Think visually, and work in different formats, including video and data visualization
  • Explain complexity clearly for readers who may know nothing about, for example, reinsurance markets
  • Tell the big picture, be able to stand back, connect events and see the larger narrative in the United States and abroad
  • Dig, be able to dive below the surface, follow the money and illuminate hidden deals and decisions  

Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years of reporting experience, ideally spanning business/economics journalism with some exposure to science, policy, or climate reporting
  • Fluency in economics and markets — you should be as comfortable reading a Fed statement as a peer-reviewed climate study
  • A track record of enterprise reporting and investigative work
  • A fluid, clear and vivid writing style; the ability to not just report but to tell a story. Good writing is a must.  
  • Demonstrated range — the ability to turn a daily news story and a 4,000-word feature with equal skill
  • Experience with public records requests, financial disclosures, or regulatory filings as reporting tools
  • Comfort with data: the ability to interrogate a dataset and recognize the story in the numbers
  •  Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Preferred Skills

  • Prior beat experience in insurance, agriculture, real estate, infrastructure, or energy markets
  • Familiarity with climate science literature and modeling (IPCC reports, NOAA/NASA data, catastrophe modeling)
  • A network of sources in insurance, banking, agribusiness, or public works

Why This Role

You'll be building something new: a beat that springs from one of the biggest stories of our time — a changing climate — with the resources, editing, and platform of The New York Times behind you. Your reporting will help readers, policymakers, and business leaders understand risks and opportunities most of the world hasn't yet digested.

*To be considered for this role, please submit your resume and cover letter, including links to 5-7 clips that demonstrate your range.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

  • Ensure coverage reflects a wide, diverse range of voices, genres, backgrounds, and ideological perspectives, and reflects the broad world of publishing, from mainstream blockbusters to important literary and non-fiction works.

  • Direct high-profile projects, including the "10 Best Books of the Year," the "100 Notable Books," and develop new books franchises, in collaboration with our newly created modern canon team.
  • Produce aggressive coverage of the publishing industry, from the economics of bookselling and marketing to debates about writing, plagiarism, artificial intelligence, ideological disputes, marquee authors and more.

You will help knit together data from different sections of the team to build our understanding of what may happen on election night throughout the year. And you will ensure we have proper observability into how data is being used.

Election Analytics is a multidisciplinary team of reporters, developers, statisticians and modelers who work on written coverage, graphics, our polls and the election-night model. This is a highly collaborative role that will involve working with colleagues from Election Analytics, the Graphics department and Interactive News.

job.title: Local Investigations Fellow
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Times is looking for reporters with a local story idea who want to investigate it under the editing guidance of Dean Baquet, The Times’s former executive editor, and a group of veteran investigative editors.

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters in local newsrooms or freelancers.

Responsibilities:

  • Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.
  • Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  1. What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  2. Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  3. Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  4. What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  5. What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  6. Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis. 

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

The New York Times Newsroom Strategy team is looking for a Strategy Manager with journalism, strategy and data experience to help shape and advance the newsroom’s biggest goals. 

This is an important and exciting moment to work in strategy at The Times. Our journalism has never been stronger or more relevant, and our newsroom continues to expand with an ever-wider array of beats, formats and expertise. At the same time, a rapidly changing media ecosystem presents significant opportunities as well as challenges, from changing audience habits to video and A.I.

The Newsroom Strategy team works with Times leaders to help the newsroom chart and implement our strategy. From coverage to audience to operations, we help identify long-term opportunities, set priorities and accomplish them. The team has helped to shape our major recent video investment; expanded our journalism with new coverage initiatives and investments in areas like Live, Well and local; and partnered with teams like Audience and Security to strengthen critical parts of our journalism operation. 

As a Manager on the team, you will lead projects, undertake analysis and recommend paths forward to ensure we are maximizing our impact. You’ll take a reporter’s eye to The Times and our priorities — spotting and investigating opportunities and challenges — and develop plans to address them. We will look to you for insightful research, data analysis and problem solving; effective partnership with stakeholders; and an enterprising and collaborative spirit. You’ll work closely with colleagues across the organization – journalists, audience and data, corporate strategy, finance, product, HR and others. 

In all your work, you’ll be rooted in our journalistic mission and the value of independence, and ensure that we are considering a wide range of perspectives from inside and outside The Times.

This role reports to the deputy editor for Newsroom Strategy and is based in New York, with regular attendance in the office at least four days each week.

Responsibilities:

  • Deliver high-quality analyses and recommendations for strategy projects: 
    • Break down complex problems and opportunities
    • Conduct research and interviews
    • Analyze quantitative and qualitative info to uncover insights
    • Ideal: Analyze data using SQL and transform big data into visualizations
    • Develop practical solutions and plans to implement them 
  • Build advisory relationships and trusting partnerships
  • Convey complex ideas in a clear and compelling way – in writing and in person
  • Operate in an enterprising and efficient manner with moderate oversight 
  • Demonstrate strong journalistic and ethical judgment, and work in accordance with our journalistic values and standards

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of relevant work experience
  • Experience in a journalism or other relevant media role
  • Experience producing strategic research and analyses, including data and financial models
  • Experience communicating recommendations to senior leaders in writing (e.g., memos, slide presentations) and verbally
  • Experience breaking down complex problems into pieces that can be solved with data, analysis, and clear assumptions
  • Passion for journalism and commitment to The Times’ mission and values 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working in a newsroom
  • Deep interest in and understanding of trends and challenges facing journalism and the media industry, and The Times in particular
  • Sound journalistic judgment, with an eye for innovative coverage opportunities 
  • Clear and concise communication style
  • Fluency in AI tools and technology
  • Technical data experience, including proficiency with SQL, comfort with version control (Github, code review), experience with dashboarding tools (Mode, Tableau, etc.) and familiarity with BigQuery or other big data environments

job.title: Reporter Fellow, Local Investigations - Mississippi, Louisiana, & Arkansas
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The Times is looking for reporters with a local story idea who want to investigate it under the editing guidance of Dean Baquet, The Times’s former executive editor, and a group of veteran investigative editors.

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters who have a local investigative story idea rooted in Louisiana, Mississippi, or Arkansas.  

This is a NY Guild role based in Louisiana, Mississippi, or Arkansas.

Responsibilities:

  • Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.
  • Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  • What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  • Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  • Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  • What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  • What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  • Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis. 

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.
